## 1. Volume Metadata Header

- **Series:** *Roots in Orbit: The NASA OSDR Plant Chronicles*

- **Volume:** 54

- **Chapter Title:** *Six Ions in the Dark*

- **OSDR Accession:** `OSD-658` (Version 7 | `GLDS-603` | DOI: `10.26030/rxc2-1v61` | Size: `204.84 GB` | Submitted: `07-Sep-2023` | Initial Release: `12-Dec-2023` | Updated: `14-Aug-2026`)

- **Primary Publication:** Dixit, A. R., Meyers, A. D., Richardson, B., Richards, J. T., Richards, S. E., Neelam, S., Levine, H. G., Cameron, M. J., & Zhang, Y. (2023). *Simulated galactic cosmic ray exposure activates dose-dependent DNA repair response and down regulates glucosinolate pathways in arabidopsis seedlings*. *Frontiers in Plant Science*, `14:1284529` (PMC10757676 | PubMed 38162303 | Frontiers | DOI: `10.3389/fpls.2023.1284529`, published `14-Dec-2023`)

- **Skipped Accessions:** `OSD-626` through `OSD-657` (contain no plant studies; `OSD-658` directly follows `OSD-625` in the plant chronology)

- **Hardware & Environment:** Ground radiation study at the **NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL)**, Brookhaven National Laboratory (Upton, NY), funded by NASA Biological and Physical Sciences (BPS) and the Human Research Program (HRP). `~100` surface-sanitized *Arabidopsis* seeds per `T25` culture flask were grown on `0.5×` MS `0.4%` phytagel (`0.5%` sucrose, `1×` Gamborg vitamins) for `8 days` (`22°C`, `40–45% RH`, `150 µmol/m²/s`, `16h/8h` photoperiod, `400–500 ppm` CO2), shipped overnight in darkness to NSRL, wrapped in `4 layers` of black tissue paper, and held in the dark for `2 days` before, during, and after beamline exposure. At `10 days` old, flasks received acute sequential **Simplified GCR Simulation** (`~20 min` total) at `0 cGy` (`n = 6`), `40 cGy` (`n = 4`), or `80 cGy` (`n = 4`), then were preserved `3 h` post-irradiation in `RNAlater` (`-80°C` after `24 h`).

- **Organism & Assay Scope:** *Arabidopsis thaliana* (`Col-0`, whole `10-day-old` seedlings, `n = 14`). RNA extracted via `Qiagen Plant RNeasy Mini Kit` (on-column DNase), `0.3 µg` input into `TruSeq Stranded Total RNA Library Prep with Ribo-Zero Globin`, sequenced across `3` runs of `75 bp` paired-end reads on **Illumina `NextSeq 550`** (`25.3M`–`38.4M` reads/sample).

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **The Six-Beam Simplified GCR Spectrum (`NSRL GCRSim`):** A `20-minute` sequential particle barrage—`35%` `1000 MeV/n H1`, `39%` `250 MeV/n H1`, `18%` `250 MeV/n He4`, `6%` `350 MeV/n O16`, `1%` `600 MeV/n Si`, and `1%` `600 MeV/n Fe56`—delivering `40 cGy` (modeling a `3.5-year` / `1,278-day` Mars transit at `~42.7 cGy` / `~1.47 Sv`) or `80 cGy` (modeling a `~6-year` Mars surface + transit mission at `~73.2 cGy`).

- **The Dose-Dependent DNA Repair Core (`RAD51`, `PARP2`, `TK1A`, `TSO2`, `SIP4`, `XRI1`):** Six DNA damage sensing and repair genes (alongside defense gene `CP1`) shared across both `40` and `80 cGy` (`FDR ≤ 0.1`) whose transcript levels scale sharply upward with radiation dose (`Kruskal-Wallis p ≤ 0.05`).

- **The `80 cGy` Heavy-Ion Checkpoint Vanguard (`BRCA1`, `PARP1`, `RAD17`, `SYN2`, `TIL1`, `AT1G49980`, `At4G19130`/`RPA`):** Homologous recombination, base excision repair, error-prone bypass (`DinB`-homolog), and `S`/mitosis cell-cycle checkpoint regulators (`CDC6`, `CDC25`, `CYCB2;3`, `EB1C`, `EMB2773`) recruited specifically when exposure doubles to `80 cGy`.

- **The Methionine-Derived Glucosinolate Pathway (`CYP79F2`, `BCAT4`, `MAM3`/`IMS2`, `IMD1`, `FMO GS-OX1`, `BAT5`, `DJ1F`, `MYB29`):** Sulfur-rich secondary metabolites (`isothiocyanate` precursors) that defend brassicas against pathogens and give radishes their spicy bite—sharply suppressed at `40 cGy` (`pathway FDR = 5.5e-10`), potentially conserving `glutathione` and `methionine` for antioxidant radioprotection.

- **The Four-Layer Black Tissue Shield (`T25` Dark-Adapted Seedlings):** Keeping seedlings in total darkness for `48 hours` strips away light-driven photoreactivation and circadian variance, isolating the raw cellular response to ionizing particles.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Beyond the Magnetosphere (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Wide Establishing):** Deep space beyond Low Earth Orbit. No blue-white magnetosphere shields the frame—only starlight and invisible cosmic ray tracks slicing through a Mars transit habitat.

- **Panel 2 (Cutaway):** Inside a transit greenhouse, `10-day-old` *Arabidopsis* seedlings sit in `0.5×` MS phytagel. On Earth, background radiation averages `2.4 mSv/year`. In deep space, plants face `1–2 mSv/day` of Galactic Cosmic Rays (`GCR`)—and half that on the Martian surface beneath `21 g/cm²` of thin atmosphere.

- **Caption:** *A 3.5-year round-trip Mars mission accumulates `~42.7 cGy` (`~1.47 Sv`). A six-year surface-and-transit campaign climbs toward `73.2 cGy`.*

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1:** Kennedy Space Center. Surface-sanitized (`70%` ethanol) `Col-0` seeds (`~100` per `T25` flask) germinate on `0.4%` phytagel (`0.5%` sucrose, `1×` Gamborg vitamins) for `8 days` at `22°C`, `150 µmol/m²/s` light (`16h/8h`).

- **Panel 2:** Overnight courier crate arriving at Brookhaven National Laboratory's **NASA Space Radiation Laboratory (NSRL)** in Upton, NY.

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "Wrap every `T25` flask in four layers of black tissue paper. Photoreactivation depends on light—if we want the pure ionizing-radiation signal, these seedlings stay in the dark."

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1:** `Day 10`. Two days into total darkness, `14` `T25` flasks are divided into three cohorts: `6` unirradiated Controls (`0 cGy`), `4` for `40 cGy`, and `4` for `80 cGy`.

- **Panel 2:** The NSRL target room. Heavy steel shielding doors slide shut; laser alignment crosshairs lock onto the dark-wrapped flasks.

- **Caption:** *Real GCRs are `85–90%` protons, `10–13%` helium ions, and `1–2%` HZE nuclei. Even `1%` heavy ions carry outsized linear energy transfer (`LET`), carving dense ionization tracks through chromatin.*

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1:** Beamline control console. The operator loads **Simplified `GCRSim`**—six sequential ion beams fired in rapid succession over `~20 minutes`.

- **Panel 2:** First pulse: `35%` `1000 MeV/n` protons (`H1`), followed immediately by `39%` `250 MeV/n` protons (`H1`).

- **SFX:** *HUMMMMMM—*

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1:** Third pulse: `18%` `250 MeV/n` helium ions (`He4`). Inside the leaf primordia, secondary delta-electrons scatter through hydrated cell walls.

- **Panel 2:** Fourth pulse: `6%` `350 MeV/n` oxygen ions (`O16`). The ionization density spikes.

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1:** Fifth and sixth pulses: `1%` `600 MeV/n` silicon (`Si`) and `1%` `600 MeV/n` iron (`Fe56`). Though only `2%` of the total dose, these HZE nuclei punch straight through nuclei like subatomic cannonballs.

- **Caption:** *Twenty minutes. Six particle species. Forty or eighty centigray absorbed.*

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor): *Track Structure in the Nucleus***

- **Visual Layout:** A dramatic two-page cross-section of a single `10-day-old` *Arabidopsis* root and cotyledon cell in pitch darkness. Across the top, six color-coded particle trajectories (`H1`, `He4`, `O16`, `Si`, `Fe56`) streak through the `TAIR10` chromatin fibers. Where `Fe56` and `Si` pass, clustered double-strand breaks (`DSBs`) and reactive oxygen species (`ROS`) flare white-hot. Beneath them, repair proteins—`PARP1/2`, `RAD51`, `BRCA1`—converge on the broken DNA ends while `RNAlater` wait-timers tick toward the `3-hour` post-irradiation mark.

- **Anchor Caption:** *Three hours post-exposure—just as repair foci peak—the black tissue is unwrapped and `RNAlater` floods all `14` flasks before freezing at `-80°C`.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1:** Case Western Reserve University's Applied Functional Genomics Core. `Qiagen Plant RNeasy` isolates total RNA; `0.3 µg` enters `TruSeq Stranded Total RNA` with `Ribo-Zero Globin`.

- **Panel 2:** Three `75 bp` paired-end runs on **Illumina `NextSeq 550`** yield `25.3M` to `38.4M` reads per sample, mapped via `STAR` (`TAIR10`) and quantified with `RSEM` and `edgeR`.

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1:** Venn diagrams split the transcriptomic storm at `p ≤ 0.01`: `472` genes of interest at `40 cGy` vs. `329` at `80 cGy`, sharing `88` GOIs.

- **Panel 2:** Under stringent `FDR ≤ 0.1`, `78` DEGs emerge at `40 cGy` (`24` up, `54` down) and `39` DEGs at `80 cGy` (`25` up, `14` down). Surprisingly, `40 cGy` triggers *far more* gene downregulation (`48` exclusive down-DEGs) than `80 cGy` (`8` exclusive down-DEGs).

### Act II: The Repair Cascade & The Checkpoint Wall (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1:** Eleven upregulated DEGs (`FDR ≤ 0.1`) are shared by both `40` and `80 cGy`. Boxplots climb in a clean staircase from `0` → `40` → `80 cGy` for `7` of them (`Kruskal-Wallis p ≤ 0.05`).

- **Panel 2:** Six of those seven stair-stepping responders are pure DNA damage machinery: **`RAD51` (`AT5G20850`)**, **`PARP2` (`AT4G02390`)**, **`TK1A` (`AT3G07800`)**, **`TSO2` (`AT3G27060`)**, **`SIP4` (`AT2G30360`)**, and **`XRI1` (`AT5G48720`)**, joined by defense gene **`CP1` (`AT5G49480`)**.

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1:** Molecular close-up on **`PARP2`**: binding broken DNA termini and ribosylating the break site to summon repair crews—activated here at *centigray* doses (`40–80 cGy`), orders of magnitude below classic `10–100 Gy` terrestrial gamma studies.

- **Panel 2:** **`RAD51`** filaments coat single-stranded DNA overhangs, searching for homologous templates to stitch double-strand breaks.

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1:** **`TK1A`** (thymidine kinase 1A) and **`TSO2`** (ribonucleotide reductase) flood the `pyrimidine` and `nucleotide metabolism` KEGG pathways (`ath00240`, `ath01232`, `FDR = 4.90E-03` at `40 cGy`; `1.38E-02` at `80 cGy`), supplying fresh dNTP bricks to patch broken chromosomes.

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1:** At `80 cGy`, the response shifts gear. Fifteen exclusive upregulated DEGs ignite, led by **`BRCA1` (`AT4G21070`)**, **`PARP1` (`AT2G31320`)**, **`RAD17` (`AT5G66130`)**, **`SYN2` (`AT5G40840`)**, **`TIL1` (`AT1G08260`)**, and **`AT1G49980`**.

- **Panel 2:** `KEGG` lights up **`Base excision repair`** (`ath03410`: `PARP1`/`APP`, `p = 1.38E-02`) and **`Homologous recombination`** (`ath03440`: `BRCA1`/`RAD51`, `p = 1.38E-02`).

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1:** `BRCA1` colocalizes with `RAD51` at DSBs, while `AT1G49980`—homolog of yeast/human `DinB` (DNA polymerase kappa)—provides error-prone translesion bypass across stubborn lesions.

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "Notice what's *missing* at `3 hours`: `ATR` doesn't budge. The `ATM`-linked network—`PARP1/2`, `BRCA1`, `RAD17`, `TSO2`, `TIL1`—is carrying the primary GCR sensing load."

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1:** Expanded `STRING` network (`p ≤ 0.01`) at `80 cGy` reveals `13` unique GO processes centered on **mitotic cell cycle** (`GO:0000278`) and **DNA repair** (`GO:0006281`, `FDR = 2.83E-08`).

- **Panel 2:** **`At4G19130`** (the `70 kDa` Replication Protein A subunit, which the authors propose formally naming **`RPA`**) bridges `RAD51`/`RAD17` repair with `CDC6`, `TIL1` (DNA Pol ε), and cohesin homologs `SYN2`/`SYN3` (`RAD21`).

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1:** Downstream mitotic gates lock down: `CDC25` and `CYCB2;3` (cyclin B2) govern `G2/M` and `M/S` transitions, while `EMB2773` (centromere assembly) and microtubule motors `EB1C`, `AT2G28620` (`RSW7`/`KIF7` homolog), and `AT5G33300` (kinesin-like) stabilize the mitotic spindle.

- **Caption:** *At `80 cGy`, the cell halts division until the heavy-ion breaks are sealed.*

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1:** Shifting focus to the `40 cGy` cohort (`62` unique GO processes): hormone and environmental stimulus pathways (`ACS11`, `BG1`) stir, while a massive metabolic shutdown sweeps across the network.

- **Panel 2:** Three shared down-DEGs drop at both doses (`p ≤ 0.05`): **`CYP79F2` (`AT1G16400`)**, **`ALDH2B7` (`AT1G23800`)**, and **`DR4` (`AT1G7333`)**.

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1:** At `40 cGy`, `48` genes plunge exclusively downward. Six belong directly to **glucosinolate biosynthesis** (`ath00966`, `FDR = 7.00E-07`): **`FMO GS-OX1`**, **`BCAT4`**, **`DJ1F`**, **`BAT5`**, **`IMD1`**, and **`MAM3`** (`IMS2`), alongside **`CYP79F2`**, **`BGLU5`**, and **`CAR7`**.

- **Panel 2:** Under `p < 0.01`, nearly *every* enzyme in aliphatic glucosinolate synthesis and sulfate assimilation (`APR`, `APS1`, `APK`) dims (`pathway FDR = 4.10E-15`).

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1:** Master transcription factor **`MYB29`** drops at both doses (`40 cGy` `LFC = -1.1`, `p = 0.003`; `80 cGy` `LFC = -0.91`, `p = 0.008`).

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "Why would `40 cGy` suppress glucosinolates *more* strongly at `3 hours` than `80 cGy`? Maybe the higher dose triggered an even faster transient dip—or `40 cGy` hits a specific metabolic triage threshold."

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1:** Inside the cytoplasm, a biochemical fork-in-the-road diagram: **Methionine** and **Glutathione** sit at the crossroads.

- **Panel 2:** Building aliphatic glucosinolates consumes both methionine (as precursor) and glutathione (as conjugate). Under ionizing `ROS` stress, shutting down glucosinolate synthesis may spare glutathione for antioxidant defense and preserve methionine for **one-carbon metabolism** and DNA methylation.

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1:** Two-sided consequence panel: **Left**, a radish and *Arabidopsis* leaf losing `isothiocyanates`—the pungent compounds that give brassicas their spicy flavor *and* fend off bacterial/fungal pathogens. **Right**, a crewed Mars greenhouse where radiation-weakened crops face heightened pathogen susceptibility.

- **Caption:** *Survival first: trade away defense and flavor to protect the genome.*

### Act III: Regolith on the Horizon (Pages 23–30)

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1:** At `80 cGy`, exclusive down-DEGs also hit **`MSRB5` (`AT4G04830`, methionine sulfoxide reductase B5)**, **`MOS9` (`AT1G12530`)**, and **`NP2` (`AT1G54960`)**, hinting at oxidative protein-repair and immune trade-offs.

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1:** A `STRING` comparison side by side: `40 cGy` (`86` GO processes, dominated by sulfur/glucosinolate repression and hormone responses) vs. `80 cGy` (`37` GO processes, dominated by `DNA repair`, `cell cycle`, and `circadian clock` clusters).

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1:** Timeline caveat card: `20 minutes` acute `GCRSim` vs. `1–2 mSv/day` chronic deep-space GCRs; `3 hours` post-exposure vs. multi-day recovery.

- **Caption:** *Acute `NSRL` beams establish the baseline—the exact early switches flipped when HZE ions strike.*

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1:** All `204.84 GB` of `OSD-658` / `GLDS-603` data—`FASTQ`s, `STAR`/`RSEM` counts, and `DESeq2`/`edgeR` tables—lock into NASA OSDR's open repository (`DOI: 10.26030/rxc2-1v61`).

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1:** A hydroponic/phytagel flask dissolves into a blueprint of a deep-space crop bay. Radiation is only one barrier; shipping terrestrial soil to Mars or the asteroids is mass-prohibitive.

- **Dialogue (Agronomist):** "We know how cosmic rays hit plant DNA on agar. Now what happens when we grow actual food crops in the *dirt* waiting for us out there?"

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1:** A sample vial of dark, carbonaceous **CI asteroid regolith simulant** pours onto a lab bench beside bags of peat moss.

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Spread): *The Carbonaceous Crust***

- **Page 29 (Panel 1):** Inside a `Percival AR-66L` growth chamber (`19.8°C–23.4°C`), three real space-crop species sprout in graded mixtures of **CI carbonaceous asteroid regolith simulant** and peat moss: **lettuce (*Lactuca sativa*)**, **radishes (*Raphanus sativus*)**, and **peppers (*Capsicum annuum*)**.

- **Page 30 (Full-Bleed Splash):** At `55 days after planting`, the simulant surface has hardened into a pale, compacted crust. High pH, low cation exchange capacity, and silt-sized particles lock out water, triggering drought stress—hitting the radishes hardest of all.

## 1. Volume Metadata Header

- **Series:** *Roots in Orbit: The NASA OSDR Plant Chronicles*

- **Volume:** 55

- **Chapter Title:** *The Carbonaceous Crust*

- **OSDR Accession:** `OSD-670` (Version 3 | `ALSDA ID: LSDS-73` | DOI: `10.26030/m04e-p031` | License: `CC0-1.0` | Size: `34.12 MB` | Submitted: `05-Oct-2023` | Initial Release: `21-May-2024` | Updated: `20-Mar-2025`)

- **Primary Publication:** Russell, S. J., Fieber-Beyer, S. K., & Yurkonis, K. A. (2022). *CI Asteroid Regolith as an In Situ Plant Growth Medium for Space Crop Production*. *The Planetary Science Journal*, `3(7):155` (UND Scholarly Commons | DOI: `10.3847/PSJ/ac74c9`, published `12-Jul-2022`)

- **Skipped Accessions:** `OSD-659` through `OSD-669` (contain no plant studies; `OSD-670` directly follows `OSD-658` in the plant chronology)

- **Hardware & Environment:** Ground study at the **University of North Dakota (UND)** Department of Biology, funded by the **North Dakota Space Grant Consortium**. Crops grew for `55 days` in a `Percival AR-66L` growth chamber (`19.8°C–23.4°C` diurnal ramp, `50–60% RH`, ambient CO2, `16 h / 8 h` photoperiod with `32 W` / `14 W` cool white fluorescent + `25 W` incandescent lamps up to `275 µmol/m²/s`, watered every other day to field capacity with distilled water). **CLASS Exolith Lab** (UCF) **CI asteroid regolith simulant** (modeled on the **Orgueil** CI carbonaceous chondrite) was tested against `SunShine` sphagnum peat moss, perlite, and commercial topsoil/vermiculite controls, plus a `2D` clinostat (`1 rotation/24 h` at `90°`). Quantitative soil chemistry was assayed at **Kansas State University Soil Testing Laboratory**.

- **Organism & Assay Scope:** Three space-crop species (`n = 83` sample records, `n = 39` photography assays): romaine lettuce (*Lactuca sativa* cv. `"Outredgeous"`), radish (*Raphanus sativus* cv. `"Pink Celebration"`), and pepper (*Capsicum annuum* cv. `"Chimayo"`), sown `5` seeds per `4-inch` pot at `~2.54 cm` depth. Measurements at `55 DAP`: germination, plant height (`cm`), dry biomass (`60°C` for `64 h`, `mg`), and `ImageJ` leaf area (`cm²`) from `iPhone SE (2nd gen)` (`28 mm`) photographs.

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **The Orgueil CI Asteroid Regolith Simulant (`CLASS Exolith Lab`):** A primordial carbonaceous chondrite analog (`48.0 wt%` Mg-serpentine, `13.5%` magnetite, `9.0%` vermiculite, `7.5%` olivine, `6.5%` pyrite, `6.0%` epsomite, `5.0%` sub-bituminous coal, `5.0%` attapulgite). Classified as a silt-based medium (`68%` silt, `26%` sand, `6%` clay) with alkaline `pH 8.1`, low `CEC` (`8.15 meq/100 g`), and high `Mg:Ca` ratio (`6,927.0` vs. `1,779.9 mg/kg`).

- **`SunShine` Sphagnum Peat Moss (`100:0` Amendment):** Acidic organic matter (`pH 4.7`, `CEC 43.98 meq/100 g`, `87.6%` organic matter) that buffers the simulant's alkalinity, boosts nitrogen (`NO3 82.4` / `NH4 129.5 mg/kg`), and physically prevents serpentine-silt crusting.

- **Radish (*Raphanus sativus* cv. `"Pink Celebration"`):** The taproot canary in the asteroid mine. Achieving `78%` overall germination, it is the only crop whose height (`4.1 cm` → `0.65 cm`) and biomass (`95.0 mg` → `15.4 mg`) collapse linearly as simulant concentration rises—choked by compaction and `P` deficiency.

- **Romaine Lettuce (*Lactuca sativa* cv. `"Outredgeous"`):** The ISS Veggie veteran (`53%` average germination). Its height and biomass hold steady across surviving treatments, yet its leaf area shrinks linearly from `2.2 cm²` (`100:0`) to `0.35 cm²` (`50:50`).

- **Pepper (*Capsicum annuum* cv. `"Chimayo"`):** The resilient opposite-leaved fruit crop (`55%` germination, `3.8 cm` mean height, `16.4 mg` biomass), showing no statistically significant drop in height, leaf area, or biomass across surviving peat-simulant ratios.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Grounding the Asteroid (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Wide Establishing):** A dark, cratered CI carbonaceous asteroid drifts through near-Earth space—the kind sampled by **Hayabusa2** (Ryugu) and **OSIRIS-REx** (Bennu).

- **Panel 2 (Inset):** Inside a laboratory jar, fine charcoal-gray powder gleams under bench lights: **CI asteroid regolith simulant** from UCF's **CLASS Exolith Lab**, engineered to match the **Orgueil** meteorite.

- **Caption:** *Resupplying prepackaged food from Earth won't scale to Mars or the asteroid belt. If crews want fresh crops off-world, they have to test the dirt already floating out there.*

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1:** University of North Dakota Biology greenhouse and `Percival AR-66L` growth chamber. Three seed packets lie side by side: **Outredgeous** romaine lettuce, **Pink Celebration** radish, and **Chimayo** pepper—representing leaf, taproot, and fruit.

- **Panel 2:** A soil-testing report from **Kansas State University** (`Project No. 31005`) spells out the simulant's paradox: `P2O5` (`0.4 wt%`) and `K2O` (`0.4 wt%`) sit in the bulk chemistry, yet plant-available nitrogen (`NO3 1.6`, `NH4 2.5 mg/kg`) and `P` (`2.8 mg/kg`) are starved—well below the `~40 mg/kg` agricultural baseline.

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1:** **Experiment A** layout: `18` `4-inch` pots per randomized complete block (`3` species × `6` substrates). Peat moss (`SunShine` sphagnum) and CI simulant step across five ratios: `100:0`, `75:25`, `50:50`, `25:75`, and `0:100` (`100%` simulant), alongside a commercial topsoil + `9 wt%` vermiculite control.

- **Panel 2:** **Experiment B** adds aeration tests: `50%` simulant / `50%` perlite, `100%` perlite, and topsoil with `25%` vermiculite / `25%` perlite.

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1:** **Experiment C**: Two pots of `5` radish seeds each in `50%` simulant / `50%` perlite mount onto twin **2-D clinostats**—one upright (`1` rotation/day control), one tilted `90°` parallel to the floor (`1 rotation/24 h` simulated microgravity).

- **Panel 2:** Five seeds drop into every pot at `~2.54 cm` (`1 inch`) depth, watered every other day to field capacity with distilled water.

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1:** Inside the `Percival AR-66L`, `32 W` and `14 W` cool white fluorescent tubes plus `25 W` incandescent bulbs ramp smoothly through sunrise, midday (`275 µmol/m²/s`), and sunset across a `16 h / 8 h` cycle (`19.8°C–23.4°C`, `50–60% RH`).

- **Panel 2:** Every other day, distilled water hits the `0:100` pure simulant pots. Instead of draining cleanly like loam, the `68%` silt particles settle and pack tight.

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1 (Close-Up):** As the surface dries between waterings, `Mg-serpentine` clay (`48.0 wt%`) filters upward, hardening into a pale **white crust** across the `0:100` and `50:50` simulant/perlite pots.

- **Caption:** *Day 10. Day 20. In `100:0` and `75:25`, green cotyledons breach the surface. In `0:100`, `50:50` simulant/perlite, and both clinostats—nothing breaks through.*

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor): *The Silt Trap***

- **Visual Layout:** A split-soil cutaway at `55 DAP`. On the left (`100:0` & `75:25` peat:simulant), loose, dark organic fibers (`pH 4.7–5.4`, `CEC 35.29–43.98 meq/100 g`) hold air pockets and moisture around vigorous radish taproots, red-tinted `Outredgeous` rosettes, and opposite-leaved `Chimayo` peppers. On the right (`0:100` pure CI simulant), the `68%` silt / `26%` sand / `6%` clay matrix collapses under water into an alkaline (`pH 8.1`), low-`CEC` (`8.15 meq/100 g`), `Mg`-heavy (`6,927 mg/kg`) brick capped by a white serpentine crust. Buried `2.54 cm` deep, ungerminated seeds suffocate from drought stress and lack of oxygen.

- **Anchor Caption:** *Zero germination in `100%` CI simulant, `50:50` simulant/perlite, and the clinostats. Even when watered every other day, compacted silt locks water and air away from the seed.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1:** Harvest at **`55 DAP`**. Researchers wash remaining substrate from every surviving root and shoot, lay dried leaves (`60°C` for `64 h`) onto centimeter graph paper, and snap `28 mm` `iPhone SE` photos for `ImageJ` red-threshold leaf-area tracing.

- **Panel 2:** `SAS PROC GLIMMIX` plots the germination curve: across all three species combined, germination drops linearly from `80%` (`100:0` / `75:25`) down to `33%` (`25:75`, `p = 0.0003`).

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1:** Species germination averages: **Radish** leads at `78%`, followed by **Pepper** (`55%`) and **Lettuce** (`53%`).

- **Dialogue (Agronomist):** "Germination tells only half the story. Watch what happens *after* they sprout."

### Act II: Three Crops, Three Fates (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1:** **Radish** (`Raphanus sativus` `"Pink Celebration"`): bright green basal rosettes shrink dramatically as simulant climbs.

- **Panel 2:** Height drops linearly from `4.1 cm` (`100:0`) to `0.65 cm` (`25:75`, `F(1,8) = 32.32`, `p = 0.0005`). Total dry biomass plunges from `95.0 mg` down to `15.4 mg` (`p = 0.0005`).

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1:** Why did radish suffer most? A cross-section of a swelling taproot pushing against dense, low-organic-matter (`14.6%` OM at `25:75` vs. `87.6%` at `100:0`) silt.

- **Caption:** *Taproots demand aeration and phosphorus (`<3 mg/kg` in pure simulant). Compacted serpentine silt starves both.*

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1:** **Romaine Lettuce** (`Lactuca sativa` `"Outredgeous"`): overall height (`1.7 cm` mean) and biomass (`11.8 mg` mean) show no significant treatment shift—until `ImageJ` measures the leaves.

- **Panel 2:** Leaf area shrinks linearly from `2.2 cm²` (`100:0`) to `0.35 cm²` (`50:50`, `p = 0.0191`), and in Block 1 the `50:50` lettuce plants die before harvest.

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1:** **Chimayo Pepper** (`Capsicum annuum`): opposite bright-green leaves stand tall (`3.8 cm` mean height, `0.80 cm²` leaf area, `16.4 mg` biomass), with `50:50` pots actually outperforming lettuce and holding steady across surviving mixes.

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "Even the `topsoil` control behaved like `≥50%` simulant—similar bulk density, plus `2.54 cm` was simply too deep for tiny lettuce seeds."

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1:** A chemical gradient bar sweeps from `100:0` peat moss to `0:100` simulant:

  - `pH`: `4.7` → `5.4` → `6.2` → `7.0` → `8.1` (alkaline lockup of micronutrients).

  - `CEC`: `43.98` → `35.29` → `33.86` → `23.38` → `8.15 meq/100 g` (leaching risk).

  - `Organic Matter`: `87.6%` → `60.8%` → `35.3%` → `14.6%` → `2.5%`.

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1:** Serpentine soil toxicity check: **Magnesium** climbs from `1,814 mg/kg` (`100:0`) to `6,927 mg/kg` (`0:100`), while **Calcium** drops from `6,028` to `1,780 mg/kg`—inverting the `Mg:Ca` ratio just like terrestrial serpentine barrens.

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1:** Side-by-side comparison table (`Table 5` of the study) pits `CI Simulant` (`P 2.8`, `K 102`, `NO3 1.6`, `pH 8.1`, `CEC 8.15`) against real carbonaceous meteorites **Murchison** (`CM2`, `P 6.0`, `K 650`, `CEC 5.8`) and **Allende** (`CV3`, `P 1,600`, `K 30`, `CEC 0.4`), plus **JSC-1A Lunar** (`P 0.2`, `K 27`, `CEC 9.6`) and **Mars-1A** (`P 0`, `K 138`, `CEC 7.3`).

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1:** Why did plants germinate in `100%` `Mars-1A` and `Mojave Mars` in earlier studies, yet fail completely in `100%` `CI` and `MGS-1`?

- **Panel 2:** Single-source volcanic-ash simulants (`Mars-1A`) vs. multi-mineral synthetic simulants (`MGS-1`, `CI`): high mineral fidelity strips out terrestrial soil microbes and decomposing organic matter, leaving a sterile, crust-prone powder.

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1:** `Experiment B` (`50%` simulant / `50%` perlite) proves perlite alone cannot rescue the crust: white serpentine clay still migrates to the top after watering, sealing the pot shut.

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1:** `Experiment C` (`2D` clinostat) closes with an honest methodological note: because both `1g` upright and `90°` microgravity clinostat pots used `50:50` simulant/perlite and suffered zero germination, `OSD-670` isolates *substrate physics* rather than microgravity effects.

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1:** Looking forward—a blueprint of UND's **NASA-funded Inflatable Lunar/Mars Habitat Plant Module**.

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "If pure CI regolith is sterile and crusts over, we don't haul chemical fertilizers from Earth. We build a *living* soil—three sisters style."

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1:** Three green-manure cover crops sketch across the blueprint: **Beans** (to fix atmospheric nitrogen into `NO3`/`NH4`), **Squash** (broad leaves to shade the silt and stop surface crusting/drought), and **Corn** (stubble tilled back in to rebuild organic carbon).

### Act III: Returning to Orbit's First Signal (Pages 23–30)

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1:** High-resolution `iPhone SE` morphometric images (`3024 × 4032 px`) and `s_OSD-670` soil tables archive into `LSDS-73` / `OSD-670` (`34.12 MB`), giving future ISRU teams exact `Melich III` and `hydrometer` baselines.

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1:** A dual-horizon closing panel: on one side, asteroid regolith waiting for nitrogen-fixing microbes; on the other, the ISS **Veggie** and **ABRS** racks where *Arabidopsis* first taught us how orbital light and gravity rewrite plant genomes.

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1:** Transition to the orbital archive: *Before crops can thrive in asteroid dirt under artificial LEDs, we still have to settle a foundational question from Low Earth Orbit.*

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1:** Telemetry rewind to **Expedition 39** on the International Space Station. Flight Engineer **Steve Swanson** tends the **CARA** (*Characterizing Arabidopsis Root Attractions*) plates—one set bathed in light, the other sealed in darkness.

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1:** Inside a cold dissection station (`4°C`), `RNAlater`-preserved seedlings thaw. Under a dissecting microscope, fine forceps separate **leaf tissues** from the hypocotyl.

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1:** Two genotypes face off: wild-type **`Col-0`** and the **`phyD`** phytochrome mutant. Earlier **CARA** work (`OSD-120`) showed `phyD` slashed differentially expressed genes in *root tips*—but what happens in the *leaves*?

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Spread): *Ten Times in the Light***

- **Page 29 (Panel 1):** Side-by-side transcriptome bars erupt from `Col-0` leaves: **light-grown** spaceflight leaves trigger **ten times** as many differentially expressed genes (`DEGs`) as **dark-grown** leaves!

- **Page 30 (Full-Bleed Splash):** Even more startling: key light-signaling, defense, and oxidative-stress pathways flip into *opposite* regulatory directions between light and darkness—proving that light isn't just energy in orbit, it is the principal conductor of the spaceflight transcriptome.

- **Cliffhanger Tag:** *Next in **OSD-678**: Light vs. Dark—and `Col-0` vs. `phyD`—in the orbital leaf transcriptome.*

- **Primary Publication:** Zhou, M., Ferl, R. J., & Paul, A.-L. (2024). *Light has a principal role in the Arabidopsis transcriptomic response to the spaceflight environment*. *npj Microgravity*, `10(1):82` (PMC11303767 | PubMed 39107298 | DOI: `10.1038/s41526-024-00417-0`, published `06-Aug-2024`)

- **Skipped Accessions:** `OSD-671` through `OSD-677` (contain no plant studies; `OSD-678` directly follows `OSD-670` in the plant chronology)

- **Hardware & Environment:** **CARA** (*Characterizing Arabidopsis Root Attractions*, CASIS `GA-2013-104`, OpNom `"Petri Plants"`), launched aboard **SpaceX CRS-3** (`04/18/2014`–`05/18/2014`) and tended on the ISS by **Expedition 39 Flight Engineer Steve Swanson**. `11-day-old` seedlings grew on phytagel Petri plates affixed directly to the **ISS US Lab bulkhead** (no dedicated plant growth hardware) vs. the **ISSES** ground control at Kennedy Space Center (`24 h` offset). **Light cohort:** constant diffuse ambient cabin light (`4–6 µmol/m²/s`). **Dark cohort:** unwrapped `4 h` to trigger germination, then sealed in blackout cloth (`24 h` dark). Harvested at `11 days` into `KFTs` with `RNAlater` (`12–18 h` ambient perfusion, then `MELFI` `-80°C`).

- **Organism & Assay Scope:** *Arabidopsis thaliana* leaves dissected at `4°C` from the exact same `CARA` plates whose root tips were archived in `OSD-120` (`n = 36`: `Col-0`, `Ws`, and `phyD` [`SALK_027956C`] × Flight/Ground × Light/Dark, `3` biological replicates/condition). `Qiagen RNeasy Plant Mini Kit`, **Illumina `NovaSeq 6000`** (`2 × 150 bp`, `54.7M–99.0M` paired-end reads/sample), mapped via `STAR v2.7.9a` (`TAIR10.51`), quantified with `HTSeq`/`DESeq2` (`|log2FC| > 1`, `Padj < 0.05`).

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **The US Lab Bulkhead & Blackout Cloth (`4–6 µmol/m²/s` vs. `0 µmol/m²/s`):** The minimalist stage of `CARA`. With no directional `Veggie` or `ABRS` LEDs, half the plates absorb weak, diffuse cabin light while their twin plates sit wrapped in blackout cloth right beside them.

- **`Col-0` & `Ws` Wild-Types:** Two *Arabidopsis* ecotypes with a hidden genetic divide—`Col-0` carries an intact red/far-red photoreceptor `PHYD`, whereas `Ws` is naturally `PHYD`-deficient.

- **Phytochrome D (`phyD`, `SALK_027956C`):** The red/far-red sensor whose loss in `Col-0` previously slashed spaceflight DEGs in *root tips* (`OSD-120`), yet in *leaves* leaves total DEG counts nearly unchanged while rewiring *which* genes fire.

- **The `LHC` Light-Harvesting Family (`25` Genes):** Photosynthetic antenna proteins that serve as the chapter's barometer of inversion—repressed in orbital light, induced in orbital darkness across all three genotypes (`0/25` genes aligned between light and dark).

- **The `GST`, `WRKY`, and `AP2/EREBP` Stress Guilds:** Oxidative, defense, and hormone-response transcription factors and transferases (`GSTU12`, `GSTU24`, `LOX2`, `JAZ8`, `RAP2.1`) whose orbital polarity flips depending on whether photons hit the leaf.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Wall-Mounted Leaves (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Wide Establishing):** Inside the **ISS US Laboratory** (*Destiny*), **Expedition 39 Flight Engineer Steve Swanson** presses Velcro-backed phytagel Petri plates directly onto the cabin bulkhead.

- **Panel 2 (Close-Up):** Beside the exposed plates—bathed in diffuse `4–6 µmol/m²/s` cabin light—an identical set of plates sits sealed inside heavy **blackout cloth** after a `4-hour` germination flash.

- **Caption:** *SpaceX CRS-3. CARA ("Petri Plants"). For eleven days, light and darkness share the exact same orbital bulkhead.*

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1:** Three genotypes line the plates (`6` plates per genotype, `11` seedlings per plate): **`Col-0`**, **`Ws`**, and **`phyD`** (`SALK_027956C`).

- **Panel 2:** At `Day 11`, Swanson slides each plate's harvest into `KFTs` filled with `RNAlater` (`12–18 h` ambient perfusion before `MELFI` `-80°C`).

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "In `OSD-120`, we sequenced the *root tips* from these exact plates. Now we're dissecting the *leaves*—from the same seedlings, same flight, same `24-hour`-offset `ISSES` ground control."

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1:** University of Florida Space Plants Lab. `RNAlater`-frozen seedlings thaw at `4°C`. Under a dissecting microscope, fine forceps snip leaf tissue cleanly from the hypocotyl.

- **Panel 2:** `Qiagen RNeasy` feeds `36` multiplexed libraries onto an **Illumina `NovaSeq 6000`** (`2 × 150 bp`, `>60M` reads/library—ranging from `54.7M` to `99.0M` reads/sample).

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1:** `STAR v2.7.9a` (`TAIR10.51`) and `DESeq2` (`|log2FC| > 1`, `Padj < 0.05`) finish the leaf-versus-root tally.

- **Panel 2:** Across all genotypes and lighting conditions, leaves erupt with **`8,477` DEGs**—dwarfing the **`716` DEGs** seen in `CARA` root tips (`OSD-120`).

- **Caption:** *Leaves are far more transcriptionally reactive to spaceflight than root tips—especially when the lights are on.*

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1:** Bar charts of `Col-0` Flight vs. Ground reveal a tenfold chasm: **light-grown `Col-0` leaves** fire **ten times** as many spaceflight DEGs as **dark-grown `Col-0` leaves**.

- **Panel 2:** Meanwhile, `phyD` leaves match `Col-0` in *total* DEG count—a sharp contrast to `phyD` root tips, where losing `PHYD` had collapsed DEG numbers.

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1:** A `6-column` expression heatmap (`Fig. 2a`) splits straight down the middle: **Light** (`Col-0`, `phyD`, `Ws` on the left) vs. **Dark** (`Col-0`, `phyD`, `Ws` on the right).

- **Caption:** *The clustering doesn't group by genotype. It groups by photons.*

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor): *The Polarity Flip***

- **Visual Layout:** A full two-page mirror spread. On the left half (**Light: `4–6 µmol/m²/s`**), `Col-0` (`4,025` DEGs), `phyD` (`4,222` DEGs), and `Ws` (`5,623` DEGs) blaze with abiotic-stress, aging, and secondary-metabolism activation while cell-wall and photosynthesis (`LHC`) pathways dim blue. On the right half (**Dark: `0 µmol/m²/s`**), the mirror image inverts: `LHC` photosynthesis genes flare red-hot, `Ws` activates hypoxia/immune pathways while repressing ion transport, and `Col-0` shows *zero* enriched down-regulated pathways.

- **Anchor Caption:** *`99.7%` (`4,014/4,025`) of `Col-0`, `99.0%` (`4,179/4,222`) of `phyD`, and `97.3%` (`5,470/5,623`) of `Ws` DEGs display distinct spaceflight patterns between light and dark. Even among genes altered in both conditions (`58` `Col-0`, `89` `phyD`, `678` `Ws`), `81%`, `52%`, and `77%` flip into opposite directions.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1:** `GenFam` enrichment across all `8,477` leaf DEGs and `716` root-tip DEGs (`Padj < 0.05`): **`GST`** (glutathione-S-transferase) and **`WRKY`** families bridge both organs, while **`LHC`** and **`AP2/EREBP`** dominate leaves.

- **Panel 2:** For all `25` **`LHC`** genes, `0%` (`0/25`) share the same regulatory direction between light and dark—every single one flips.

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1:** Over `90%` of `GST`, `AP2/EREBP`, and `WRKY` DEGs in leaves (and `GST` in root tips) follow distinct light/dark trajectories. Only `Col-0` root-tip `WRKY` genes (`17%` distinct) act largely independent of light.

### Act II: The `PHYD` & Ecotype Rewiring (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1:** Why did `phyD` leaves have almost as many DEGs as `Col-0`? Overlap analysis (`Fig. 5a`) isolates **`PHYD`-dependent spaceflight-altered genes**—genes equal on Earth (`Ground`) that diverge *only* in orbit in `Col-0`, remaining flat in `phyD`.

- **Panel 2:** In the **Light**, **`71` `PHYD`-dependent genes** emerge (`63` up, `8` down): e.g., **`GSTU12`** surges in `Col-0` flight leaves while **`LOX2`** (lipoxygenase 2, green-leaf volatile synthesis) drops—both frozen in `phyD`.

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1:** In the **Dark**, **`28` `PHYD`-dependent genes** emerge (`20` up, `8` down): e.g., **`LHCA1`** rises and auxin-responsive **`AT3G61840`** falls in `Col-0` flight leaves, but not in `phyD`.

- **Panel 2:** Venn diagram between Light (`71`) and Dark (`28`) `PHYD`-dependent genes: **`0` overlap**. `PHYD` steers completely separate gene sets in light versus darkness.

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1:** Next, `Col-0` vs. **`Ws`**—an ecotype naturally deficient in `PHYD`. In the **Light**, **`486` `Ws`-deficient** spaceflight genes respond only in `Col-0` (`ABC` transporters, `GST` [`GSTU24` up, `GSTU18` down], `NAC`, `WRKY`).

- **Panel 2:** Conversely, **`292` `Col-0`-deficient** genes respond only in `Ws`—including abiotic stress responders **`DES1`** (up) and **`CBF1`** (down).

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1:** In the **Dark**, **`51` `Ws`-deficient** genes (`LHCA2`, `GSTU15`) respond only in `Col-0`, while **`408` `Col-0`-deficient** genes (`AP2/EREBP` [`RAP2.1`], `SWEET` sugar transporters, jasmonate repressor `JAZ8`) fire only in `Ws`.

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1:** Connecting `phyD` and `Ws`: **`~43%`** of `PHYD`-dependent spaceflight genes (`31/71` in light, `12/28` in dark) are *also* `Ws`-deficient—confirming `PHYD`'s shared genetic footprint across ecotypes.

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1:** `Metascape` pathway summary (`Fig. 9`) contrasts Earth vs. Orbit. On Earth, core stress genes (`HY5`, `CBF`, `PIF4`, `HSP70`, `PR1`) keep the same sign regardless of light.

- **Dialogue (Researcher):** "In space, there is no universal 'spaceflight gene.' Plants recruit the same *families*—defense, oxidative stress, light signaling, secondary metabolism—but light dictates which way the switches flip."

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1:** Comparing `CARA`'s diffuse `4–6 µmol/m²/s` bulkhead lighting against `Veggie`, `ABRS`, `EMCS`, `BRIC`, `SJ-10`, and `TG-2`: weak, non-directional cabin light removes both gravity *and* strong phototropism, amplifying leaf sensitivity.

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1:** In the **Light**, leaves activate abiotic stress and aging pathways while repressing cell-wall organization and cell-cycle programs.

- **Panel 2:** In the **Dark**, lacking both gravity and photons, leaves induce ethylene/jasmonic acid signaling (`JAZ8`) and shut down ion transport and chemical homeostasis.

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1:** `phyD` and `Ws` prove that losing `PHYD` doesn't kill the plant in orbit—instead, it forces the leaf to rewire around a different subset of stress pathways, potentially altering metabolic cost.

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1:** Engineering takeaway card: *Any future CRISPR or breeding target for space crops must be paired with the exact light spectrum and intensity it will grow under.*

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1:** All `1.47 TB` of `CARA` leaf RNA-Seq reads lock into `PRJNA1069768` and `OSD-678` (`GLDS-612`), completing the paired leaf-and-root (`OSD-120`) atlas of `SpaceX CRS-3`.

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1:** Montage of the series' journey so far: from `BRIC` canisters and `Veggie` pillows (`OSD-625`, `OSD-678`), through `NSRL` cosmic-ray beams (`OSD-658`) and asteroid regolith (`OSD-670`).

### Act III: Silver in the Water (Pages 23–30)

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1:** Transition to NASA Kennedy Space Center's **Space Station Processing Facility (SSPF)** (`Percival PGW-48` growth chambers).

- **Dialogue (Life Support Engineer):** "Light and regolith are solved only if our *water loop* doesn't poison the greenhouse."

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1:** Spacecraft potable water systems rely on **ionic silver (`Ag+`)** as a biocide—designed to dose between **`200` and `500 ppb`** (`0.2–0.5 mg/L`), with `100 ppb` as the drinking-water threshold.

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1:** **Outredgeous** romaine lettuce (*Lactuca sativa*) grows in two parallel setups: **arcillite** substrate vs. **pure hydroponics** trays—challenged with `0`, `31`, `125`, and `500 ppb` `Ag+`.

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1:** `108` hydroponic water samples are concentrated on a `CP SELECT (0.20 µm)` instrument alongside `192` shoot and root tissues (`48` arcillite shoots/roots, `48` hydroponic shoots/roots) for `NextSeq 1000` metagenomics.

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1:** In **arcillite**, cation-exchange capacity buffers the silver—the root-zone microbiome's alpha diversity and relative abundance barely flinch.

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1:** In **hydroponics**, with zero cation-exchange capacity, ionic silver strikes exposed roots directly. Above **`31 ppb` `Ag+`**, lettuce growth stunts severely.

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Spread): *The Stringent Response***

- **Page 29 (Panel 1):** Stunted hydroponic roots leak carbon exudates into the silver-laced tray water, triggering a selective microbial bloom as alpha diversity rises with `Ag+` concentration.

- **Page 30 (Full-Bleed Splash):** Metagenomic pathways light up across the surviving root-zone microbiome: alternate carbon utilization, fatty-acid synthesis, and the **`ppGpp`** (*guanosine 3'-diphosphate 5'-diphosphate*) **stringent response** global stress system.

- **Cliffhanger Tag:** *Next in **OSD-723**: Substrate matters—when spacecraft potable-water silver meets hydroponic lettuce.*

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **Dr. Aubrie O'Rourke (KSC ER&T Lead Investigator):** Principal corresponding author at NASA Kennedy Space Center's Exploration Research and Technology Division; designs the `AgFoam`-to-lettuce crossover to test whether future spacecraft potable water (`200–500 ppb` `Ag⁺`) can safely irrigate spaceflight crops without pre-filtration.

- **LaShelle Spencer (LASSO II / Noetic Strategies Crop Lead):** First author and experimental supervisor inside the SSPF `Percival PGW-48` chambers; oversees the 28-day arcillite vs. `Crop King` NFT grow-outs, daily `pH 5.7–5.8` / `EC 1.2 mS/cm` adjustments, and `LI-3100C` / `SPAD-502DL` / `ACM-200 Plus` phenotyping.

- **Dr. Raymond Wheeler (KSC Senior Plant Physiologist):** Co-conceptualizer and supervisor bridging Veggie/APH arcillite heritage with next-generation substrate-free hydroponics (`PWM`, `XROOTS`).

- **The `Ag⁺` Ion Stream (`0 / 31 / 125 / 500 ppb`):** Unbound silver cations leached from the `290 mL` `AgFoam` (`AgClNP`) cartridge—benign to crew at potable doses, yet fiercely reactive in solution against plastocyanin `Cu⁺` binding, essential nutrient uptake, and bacterial membranes.

- **The Cation-Exchange Shield (Arcillite vs. Rockwool/NFT):** Negatively charged calcined clay particles (`Turface`) that adsorb and immobilize `Ag⁺` before it reaches the root cortex, contrasted against bare `Grodan` rockwool and recirculating NFT channels with near-zero cation-exchange capacity.

- **The Surviving Rhizosphere Guild (`Cupriavidus`, `Sphingomonas`, `Sphingobium`, `Ralstonia`, `Novosphingobium`):** Waterborne genera selected under `125` and `500 ppb` `Ag⁺` stress—rewiring their metabolism toward fatty-acid membrane repair, the glyoxylate bypass, phytol degradation, and the `ppGpp` stringent response alarmone while feeding on exudates from stunted lettuce roots.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: The Potable Paradox (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Full-width establishing shot):** Exterior of the Space Station Processing Facility (SSPF) at NASA Kennedy Space Center under a humid Florida dawn; high-bay shadows stretch across the concrete apron.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up):** A `290 mL` polypropylene in-line `AgFoam` cartridge rests on a stainless lab bench beside a `20 L` sterile carboy. Deionized water pulses through the polyurethane–silver chloride nanoparticle (`AgClNP`) matrix.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *On the International Space Station, iodine (`I₂`) keeps potable water clean—until you have to strip it out before the crew drinks, lest it wreck their thyroids.*

- **Panel 3 (Medium shot):** Aubrie O'Rourke watches the digital readout of a silver ion-selective electrode (ISE) stabilize at `500 ppb`.

- **Aubrie O'Rourke:** "Exploration spacecraft won't strip silver. The potable water dispenser is spec'd for `200` to `500 ppb` `Ag⁺`—straight to the tap, and straight to the plant chambers."

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1 (Two-shot):** Raymond Wheeler and LaShelle Spencer stand before the glowing banks of `Percival PGW-48` growth chambers inside the SSPF.

- **LaShelle Spencer:** "Veggie and APH buffer their roots in arcillite—calcined clay with high cation-exchange capacity. But `PWM` and `XROOTS` are pushing substrate-free hydroponics to cut up-mass and hypoxia."

- **Panel 2 (Technical inset):** Side-by-side schematic of the two worlds: `Turface` calcined clay granules bristling with negative surface charges vs. an open `Crop King` Nutrient Film Technique (`NFT`) trough flowing over `Grodan` rockwool.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "If `Ag⁺` has nothing to bind to, it hits the root surface naked."

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1 (Wide interior):** Inside the `Percival PGW-48` chamber (`101 kPa`, `23°C`, `50% RH`), a `3000 ppm` CO₂ sensor ticks steadily. Overhead LEDs (`450 nm`, `660 nm`, `730 nm`, `6000 K` white) bathe the racks in a sharp magenta-white glare (`300 µmol/m²/s`, `16 h` light / `8 h` dark).

- **Panel 2 (Detail):** Chlorine-gas-sanitized seeds of *Lactuca sativa* cv. `'Outredgeous'`—four per `9 × 10.2 cm` pot in autoclaved arcillite amended with `7.5 g/L` `T70 16-6-8 Nutricote`, and two per `Grodan` rockwool cube in the `NFT` channels.

- **Panel 3 (Action):** Clear germination domes settle over the `1020` trays and `NFT` troughs.

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1 (Grid of four carboys):** Four `0.22 µm`-filtered sterile carboys lined up with spigots labeled `0 ppb (Control)`, `31 ppb`, `125 ppb` (just above the `100 ppb` EPA drinking-water limit), and `500 ppb` (the spacecraft dispenser ceiling).

- **Panel 2 (Medium shot):** LaShelle Spencer and Tesia Irwin check `pH` and `EC` meters beside the `NFT` reservoirs; a dropper of `1 M` nitric acid (`HNO₃`) poises above the `0.5× Hoagland's/Arnon` nutrient stream.

- **LaShelle Spencer:** "`pH` locked at `5.7` to `5.8`. `EC` at `1.2 mS/cm`. Fresh weekly changeouts so silver never plates out unnoticed."

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1 (Calendar montage, Days 1–7):** Clear domes lift as true leaves emerge; seedlings are thinned to one per pot or plug. In arcillite, all four treatments uncurl crisp, even cotyledons.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up, `NFT` `500 ppb`):** In the hydroponic trough, germination lags. Emerging radicles hesitate at the wet rockwool edge as silver ions drift unhindered through the `0.5× Hoagland's` film.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *Three full grow-outs. Two systems per treatment. Eight plants per system. `48` lettuce plants per dose—`28` days to crew-edible maturity.*

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1 (Wide chamber shot, Day 14):** The randomized tray layout across the `Percival` shelf reveals a stark visual split. On the arcillite side, `'Outredgeous'` rosettes swell uniformly across `0`, `31`, `125`, and `500 ppb`.

- **Panel 2 (Low-angle shot, `NFT` side):** On the hydroponic side, `31 ppb` plants already lag behind `0 ppb` controls. At `125 ppb` and `500 ppb`, miniature rosettes hug the rockwool, their leaves flushing deep, stressed crimson.

- **Aubrie O'Rourke:** "Look at the anthocyanin flush. That's not normal `'Outredgeous'` pigmentation—that's an antioxidant alarm."

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor: *The Electrostatic Divide*)**

- **Left Page (Page 7) — *The Clay Shield (Arcillite, `500 ppb`)*:** Cross-section through a `Turface` arcillite pore at microscopic scale. Positively charged `Ag⁺` ions stream in with the irrigation water, only to snap onto negatively charged aluminosilicate clay surfaces like iron filings onto a magnet. Beneath the shielded clay grains, a healthy `'Outredgeous'` root hair absorbs `Ca²⁺`, `K⁺`, phosphate, and sulfate unimpeded.

- **Right Page (Page 8) — *The Unbuffered Flood (`NFT` Hydroponics, `500 ppb`)*:** Cross-section through a bare `Grodan` rockwool fiber and `NFT` water film. With no cation-exchange capacity to trap them, `Ag⁺` ions swarm the root epidermis directly—displacing `Ca`, `K`, `P`, and `S` transport, infiltrating the xylem toward leaf chloroplasts (threatening `Cu⁺` binding in plastocyanin), while stressed roots bleed carbon exudates into the flowing film.

- **Spread Caption:** *Same water. Same `3000 ppm` CO₂. Same `28` days. The only difference is whether the substrate catches the bullet.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1 (Medium shot, Day 28 Harvest):** Harvesting day at the SSPF benches. `LI-3100C` leaf area meter, `SPAD-502DL` chlorophyll meter, and `ACM-200 Plus` anthocyanin meter sit ready beside `50 mL` conical tubes and a smoking Dewar of liquid nitrogen.

- **Panel 2 (Data readout):** In arcillite: zero significant differences across `0`, `31`, `125`, and `500 ppb` in plant height, plant area, shoot fresh mass, shoot dry mass, leaf area, leaf number, chlorophyll, or anthocyanin.

- **Panel 3 (Data readout):** In hydroponics: height, area, fresh mass, dry mass, leaf area, and leaf number all collapse (`p ≤ 0.001` at `31`, `125`, and `500 ppb`), while anthocyanin spikes (`p ≤ 0.001`) at `125` and `500 ppb`.

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1 (Action):** Blake Costine and Angie Diaz flash-freeze harvested shoots, roots, and `50 mL` weekly `NFT` water aliquots (`0, 7, 14, 21, 28 DAP`) into liquid nitrogen for `-80°C` storage.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up):** A Krups `One-Touch Grinder` and mortar and pestle pulverize `0.20–0.26 g` dried leaf tissue for acid digestion (`70% HNO₃` + `30% H₂O₂` at `95°C`) before `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES elemental profiling.

- **LaShelle Spencer:** "Stunting is only half the question. If the crew eats these leaves, how much silver actually made it into the salad?"

### Act II: The Elemental Swap & The Resistant Guild (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1 (Wide lab shot):** Inside the analytical lab, the Thermo Fisher `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES plasma torch flares white-hot as `0.2 µm`-filtered digests aspirate into the spray chamber.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up, arcillite readouts):** Arcillite leaf spectra flatline at zero for silver across all treatments—`Ag⁺` never left the clay. `Ca`, `K`, `Fe`, `P`, and `S` remain rock-steady.

- **Panel 3 (Close-up, hydroponic readouts):** Hydroponic leaves light up: `Ag⁺` registers across all three doses, peaking at a mean **`7 µg/g` dry weight (`7000 ppb`)** under `125 ppb` irrigation (`p ≤ 0.05`) and **`4 µg/g` dry weight (`4000 ppb`)** at `500 ppb`.

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1 (Bar-chart overlay):** As `Ag⁺` climbs inside hydroponic leaves, essential macronutrients plummet in lockstep: calcium (`p ≤ 0.05` at `125 ppb`, `p ≤ 0.01` at `500 ppb`), potassium (`p ≤ 0.001`), phosphorus (`p ≤ 0.01`), and sulfur (`p ≤ 0.01`) all drop sharply against `0 ppb` controls.

- **Panel 2 (Two-shot):** Aubrie O'Rourke checks the Eurofins HPLC vitamin report (`AOAC 942.23`, `967.22`): vitamin K1 (phylloquinone) and vitamin C (ascorbic acid) hold steady, while thiamine HCl and K2 vitamers remain below detection.

- **Panel 3 (Calculation):** A notepad calculation: `0.2 g` dry (`5 g` fresh) stunted shoot carries `~1.1 µg` `Ag⁺`, meaning a `50 kg` astronaut could eat `~40` stunted heads before hitting ECHA's `0.9 µg/kg/day` ADI.

- **Aubrie O'Rourke:** "Chemically safe in tiny bites—but agronomically useless. You can't feed a crew on thumb-sized lettuce starved of calcium and potassium."

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1 (Transition):** Shift to the molecular genomics bench. `108` hydroponic tray water samples pass through the `InnovaPrep CP SELECT` (`0.20 µm` hollow-fiber concentrator) and elute into `750 µL` of `0.075%` Tween 20/Tris buffer.

- **Panel 2 (Detail):** Alongside them, `100 mg` aliquots of `48` arcillite shoots, `48` arcillite roots, `48` hydroponic shoots, and `48` hydroponic roots undergo `ZymoBIOMICS` DNA extraction, followed by `NEBNext` host-DNA depletion (`1 µg` input) and `Illumina DNA Prep` UDI library construction.

- **Panel 3 (Wide):** Inside the KSC sequencing suite, an `Illumina NextSeq 1000` hums through `2 × 150 bp` paired-end runs across `312` FASTQ pairs (`22.75 GB` deposited to `OSD-723` / `GLDS-645`).

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1 (Bioinformatics terminal):** Anirudha Dixit and Cory Spern run `FastQC v0.12.1`, `MultiQC v1.17`, and `HoCoRT v1.2.2` to strip plant and human reads, feeding `315` clean microbial read files into the NASA GeneLab `HUMAnN3 v3.6` / `MetaPhlAn3 v4.0.1` pipeline.

- **Panel 2 (Data filter):** `126` of `312` samples pass the `> 1` classified genus threshold: `43/48` arcillite roots, `10/12` arcillite water controls, `27/48` hydroponic roots, `36/108` hydroponic water samples—and only `6/48` arcillite shoots and `5/48` hydroponic shoots.

- **Anirudha Dixit:** "Shoots are microbial deserts in both systems. The real story is underwater."

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1 (Shannon diversity plots):** In arcillite roots, alpha diversity is high and completely unbothered by `0`, `31`, `125`, or `500 ppb` `Ag⁺`. Irrigation water carries `Sphingomonas` or `Methylobacterium`, while roots and shoots are dominated by seed-borne `Pseudomonas`, `Massilia` (`Maxilla`), `Ralstonia`, `Methylobacterium`, `Cupriavidus`, and `Herbaspirillum`.

- **Panel 2 (Contrast):** In hydroponics, the pattern flips upside down. Control (`0 ppb`) water starts with higher diversity than silver-treated water—but on the hydroponic **roots** and in the **tray water at Day 28**, Shannon alpha diversity *climbs* as `Ag⁺` rises (`31 ppb` vs. `500 ppb` roots, `p < 0.05`; all `Ag⁺` water trays vs. `0 ppb`, `p < 0.05`).

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1 (Time-series graph, Weeks 1–4):** Weekly `NFT` water sampling reveals a creeping recovery: Weeks 1, 2, and 3 silver treatments sit below `0 ppb` controls in alpha diversity, yet climb steadily every week despite complete weekly water changeouts—until by Week 4, silver-treated water matches the control's diversity.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up, Aubrie O'Rourke):** Her eyes narrow at the Week 4 convergence.

- **Aubrie O'Rourke:** "Heavy metals in soil usually *crush* root diversity. Why is silver *increasing* diversity on hydroponic roots over four weeks?"

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1 (Microscopic visualization):** A stunted `500 ppb` hydroponic root tip sloughs cap cells and leaks sugars, amino acids, and organic acids—the *rhizosphere effect* under chemical siege.

- **Panel 2 (Relative abundance stacked bars):** In `125` and `500 ppb` hydroponic roots and tray water, the same five waterborne genera recur: `Sphingomonas`, `Sphingobium`, `Ralstonia`, `Novosphingobium`, and `Cupriavidus`.

- **Panel 3 (Directional arrows):** At `500 ppb`, `Novosphingobium` drops on roots relative to tray water—while heavy-metal-tolerant `Cupriavidus` surges onto the root surface.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *Silver isn't sterilizing the `NFT` tray. It's filtering it—driving waterborne survivors to shelter in root biofilms.*

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1 (Venn diagram, `DESeq2` `log2FC ≥ 2.5`, `p ≤ 0.01`):** Comparing silver-treated hydroponic roots against `0 ppb` controls: `31 ppb` shows **zero** enriched bacterial pathways. `125 ppb` and `500 ppb` share **13** overlapping enriched pathways—and `500 ppb` unlocks **12** additional stress-specific pathways.

- **Panel 2 (Metabolic diagram):** The `13` shared pathways light up: branched-chain amino acid synthesis (`VALSYN-PWY`, `ILEUSYN-PWY`), anaerobic oleate/dodecenoate/palmitoleate fatty-acid biosynthesis (`PWY-7664`, `PWY0-862`, `PWY-6282`), `GLYOXYLATE-BYPASS`, and `PWY66-389` (phytol degradation).

- **Anirudha Dixit:** "Silver punches holes in bacterial membranes—so the survivors crank up fatty-acid synthesis to patch their envelopes, and switch to the glyoxylate cycle and phytol degradation to eat plant-derived carbon."

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1 (Zoom into the `500 ppb`-exclusive circle):** At the center of the `12` pathways unique to `500 ppb` glows `PPGPPMET-PWY`: **`ppGpp`** (*guanosine 3'-diphosphate 5'-diphosphate*) metabolism.

- **Panel 2 (Molecular inset):** The bacterial stringent-response alarmone `ppGpp` locks onto transcriptional machinery, throttling growth and shifting the cell into armored survival mode.

- **Aubrie O'Rourke:** "No antibiotic resistance genes enriched—but `ppGpp` stringent response, membrane lipid remodeling, and biofilm carbon-scavenging. Give subinhibitory silver enough weeks, and the biocide trains its own survivors."

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1 (Comparison glance, Arcillite pathways):** Even in arcillite—where the lettuce looked untouched—all three `Ag⁺` doses enriched `ECASYN-PWY` (enterobacterial common antigen biosynthesis) in root-associated Enterobacteriaceae, while `125`/`500 ppb` dipped `NAD-BIOSYNTHESIS-II`.

- **Panel 2 (Two-shot):** Wenyan Li and Christina Khodadad review the full `309`-sample matrix.

- **Wenyan Li:** "So the clay protected the plant completely, even while the root-zone microbes quietly noticed the trace silver."

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1 (Wide SSPF lab):** The `Percival PGW-48` doors swing open after the third and final grow-out. Stainless trays gleam under the overhead white fluorescent lights.

- **Panel 2 (Side-by-side tray photo recreation):** `28`-day arcillite `'Outredgeous'` heads—lush, broad, burgundy-tipped rosettes—sit beside `28`-day `500 ppb` `NFT` lettuce heads no bigger than a silver dollar.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "There's our design rule for Artemis and Mars transit greenhouses."

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1 (Close-up, whiteboard):** Aubrie O'Rourke writes the threshold in bold marker: **HYDROPONICS: `< 31 ppb Ag⁺` REQUIRED (OR PRE-FILTER / USE HIGH-CEC SUBSTRATE).**

- **Panel 2 (Medium shot):** Trent Smith and Michael Callahan's life-support notes sit beside the whiteboard—connecting potable water hardware specs (`200–500 ppb` `Ag⁺`) directly to crop-chamber plumbing.

- **Aubrie O'Rourke:** "If a spacecraft lacks cation-exchange media, `200` to `500 ppb` silver water will cripple its greenhouse before the first harvest."

### Act III: The Clean-Water Mandate & The Orbital Salad (Pages 23–30)

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1 (Detail):** The `AgFoam` cartridge is uncoupled from the `NFT` manifold and set beside a clean ion-exchange resin column.

- **Panel 2 (Caption):** *For `APh` and Veggie—which prime their tanks with potable water but rely on arcillite—`500 ppb` `Ag⁺` poses no threat to lettuce yield, elemental nutrition, or root-zone alpha diversity.*

- **Panel 3 (Caption):** *For substrate-free `PWM` or `XROOTS` hydroponics, silver must be scrubbed below `31 ppb` before irrigation—and water loops monitored against `Cupriavidus` biofilm selection.*

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1 (Data upload screen):** `OSD-723` / `GLDS-645` (`DOI: 10.26030/nvwv-qm40`) packages `312` paired-end metagenomic FASTQs (`22.75 GB`), ICP-OES elemental tables, and vitamin HPLC assays into NASA OSDR.

- **Panel 2 (Journal masthead):** *Microorganisms* (`12(3):515`, March 4, 2024) locks the findings into the permanent space-biology record.

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1 (Silhouette):** Inside the darkened SSPF chamber bay, the `Percival` LEDs cycle into their `8 h` night phase. Only the status LEDs on the `CO₂` controller pulse green.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up):** A single `'Outredgeous'` leaf from the `0 ppb` control tray rests on a sterile weigh boat—crisp, turgid, unblemished.

- **LaShelle Spencer:** "We know what ground-chamber silver does to `'Outredgeous'`. Now think about what's already been harvested upstairs."

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1 (Memory flash):** Orbital daylight over the International Space Station cupola; inside the Columbus/Express rack, the pink-magenta glow of **Veggie** (`VEG-01A`, `VEG-01B`, `VEG-03A`) illuminates floating red romaine leaves.

- **Panel 2 (Astronaut silhouettes):** Steve Swanson, Scott Kelly, Kjell Lindgren, and Shane Kimbrough tending the root pillows in microgravity—no `Ag⁺` biocide, just flight-certified Veggie hardware and orbital radiation.

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1 (Lab bench transition):** Frozen flight-returned `'Outredgeous'` leaves from ISS Veggie expeditions sit beside ground-control twins—destined not for metagenomic `Ag⁺` stress, but for a full **nutritional and food-safety reckoning**.

- **Panel 2 (Equipment close-up):** An `ASE 350` accelerated solvent extractor, `Folin-Ciocalteu` phenolic reagents, `ORAC` antioxidant fluorometer wells (`Trolox`/`AAPH`), and the `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES stand ready.

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1 (Microbiology plate):** Nutrient agar and yeast/mold plates show colony counts ranging from `2.14` to `4.86 log₁₀ CFU/g`—clean of select human pathogens, yet carrying subtle shifts in `VEG-03A` leaf bacterial genera between spaceflight and Earth.

- **Panel 2 (ICP-OES readout):** Even without silver in the water, flight-grown ISS lettuce diverges from ground controls in `Fe`, `K`, `Na`, `P`, `S`, and `Zn`—while anthocyanins and `ORAC` antioxidant capacity hold steady.

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Double-Page Spread: *Next Station — `OSD-745`*)**

- **Left Page (Page 29):** Inside the ISS, an astronaut clips a fresh `'Outredgeous'` leaf from a `VEG-03A` pillow under pink LEDs, holding it up against the Earth's blue limb outside the window.

- **Right Page (Page 30):** Split-screen data cascade linking the KSC ground chamber (`OSD-723`) to the orbital Veggie archive (`OSD-745`): phenolic assays (`Folin-Ciocalteu`), `ORAC` curves, `iCAP 7000` trace elements (`Fe, K, Na, P, S, Zn`), and `2.14–4.86 log₁₀ CFU/g` leaf microbiota.

- **Spread Caption:** *Silver taught us how substrate guards the root. Next, we open the ISS Veggie harvest log itself—to ask what microgravity actually puts on an astronaut's plate.*

- **Cliffhanger Tag:** **NEXT VOLUME: `OSD-745` — *Microbiological and Nutritional Analysis of Lettuce Crops Grown on the International Space Station*.**

## 4. Mission Debrief (Pages 31–32 Infographic Layout)

### Left Spread — Page 31: Experimental Matrix & Plant/Elemental Outcomes (`OSD-723`)

| Parameter / Metric | Arcillite (`Turface` + `Nutricote`) | Hydroponics (`Grodan` + `NFT`) | Statistical & Biological Takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Substrate & CEC** | Calcined clay (high cation-exchange capacity) | Rockwool + `0.5× Hoagland's` (no CEC) | Clay adsorbs `Ag⁺`; `NFT` leaves `Ag⁺` bioavailable |
| **Growth at `31 ppb` `Ag⁺`** | No significant difference vs. `0 ppb` | Reduced height, area, mass, leaf count (`p ≤ 0.001`) | `31 ppb` is already toxic in unbuffered `NFT` |
| **Growth at `125` & `500 ppb`** | Normal `28`-day `'Outredgeous'` rosettes | Severely stunted; anthocyanin spike (`p ≤ 0.001`) | `200–500 ppb` potable spec cripples `NFT` crops |
| **Leaf `Ag⁺` Accumulation** | Not detected (`0 µg/g`) across all doses | Detected at all doses (`7 µg/g` DW at `125 ppb`) | Clay blocks foliar `Ag⁺` translocation completely |
| **Essential Elements & Vitamins** | `Ca, K, Fe, P, S`, Vit `K1`, Vit `C` unchanged | `Ca, K, P, S` drop (`p ≤ 0.05` to `≤ 0.001`); Vit `K1`/`C` stable | `Ag⁺` uptake inversely impairs macronutrient uptake |

### Right Spread — Page 32: Root/Water Microbiome & Metagenomic Pathways (`OSD-723`)

| Assay / Feature | Arcillite Response (`0–500 ppb` `Ag⁺`) | Hydroponic `NFT` Response (`0–500 ppb` `Ag⁺`) | Mechanism / Spaceflight Implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Alpha Diversity (Shannon)** | High in roots, unchanged across `Ag⁺` doses | Increases with `Ag⁺` in roots & Week 4 tray water (`p < 0.05`) | Waterborne survivors adapt over `4` weeks despite changeouts |
| **Dominant Taxa** | Seed-derived `Pseudomonas`, `Massilia`, `Ralstonia`, `Methylobacterium` | Water-driven `Sphingomonas`, `Sphingobium`, `Ralstonia`, `Novosphingobium`, `Cupriavidus` | `Cupriavidus` enriches on `500 ppb` roots vs. tray water |
| **Shared Pathways (`125` & `500 ppb`)** | `ECASYN-PWY` (`>2.5 log2FC` in all `Ag⁺` doses) | `13` shared pathways: fatty-acid (`palmitoleate`/`oleate`), `VALSYN`/`ILEUSYN`, glyoxylate, phytol | Membrane repair + scavenging exudates from stunted roots |
| **High-Dose Pathway (`500 ppb` only)** | `NAD-BIOSYNTHESIS-II` decreased (`125` & `500 ppb`) | `12` unique pathways including `PPGPPMET-PWY` (`ppGpp`) | Stringent response global regulatory stress alarmone |
| **Sequencing Scope (`GLDS-645`)** | `48` shoots, `48` roots, `12` water controls | `48` shoots, `48` roots, `108` water samples (`0–28 DAP`) | `NextSeq 1000` (`2×150 bp`); `126/312` samples `>1` genus |
