- **Skipped Accessions:** `OSD-724` through `OSD-744` (contain no plant studies)

- **Hardware & Environment:** International Space Station (`ISS-Columbus`) **Vegetable Production System (Veggie)** (`VEG-01A` `May 8–Jun 10, 2014`; `VEG-01B` `Jul 8–Aug 10, 2015`; `VEG-03A` `Oct 25–Dec 28, 2016`; `SpaceX-3` & `SpaceX-8`) vs. KSC controlled-environment ground controls (`24 h` delay for `VEG-01A`/`B`, `72 h` delay for `VEG-03A`); `6` arcillite rooting pillows (`Turface Proleague` + `Nutricote 18-6-8`, `25 mL` initial hydration, `23.25°C` mean); LED array `30.5–31.75 cm` above baseplate (`~200 µmol/m²/s` PAR, `12:3:1` red `630 nm` : blue `455 nm` : green `530 nm`, `16:8` light:dark).

- **Organism & Assay Scope:** *Lactuca sativa* cv. `'Outredgeous'` (`33` days single harvest for `VEG-01A`/`B`; `33–56+` days sequential "cut-and-come-again" harvests for `VEG-03A`; `n = 60` samples in `OSD-745`); **Anthocyanin Content** (`ASE 350` + `Beckman DU 700` at `530`/`650 nm`), **Phenolic Content** (`ASE 350` + `Folin-Ciocalteu` on `BioTek Synergy Hybrid`), **ORAC** (`AWA` extraction, `Trolox`/`AAPH`, `BioTek Synergy Hybrid`), **Elemental Analysis** (`iCAP 7000` ICP-OES, EPA 3050B mod.), **Photography** (`NIKON D4S`), and companion heterotrophic plate counts & `Illumina MiSeq` `16S`/`ITS` community profiling (`PMC7067979`).

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **Dr. Gioia Massa (KSC Veggie Project Lead):** Conceptualization lead for Veggie hardware validation (`VEG-01A`, `VEG-01B`, `VEG-03A`); orchestrates the transition from Earth-bound plant-pillow engineering to the first astronaut-consumed salad in orbit.

- **Dr. Christina L. M. Khodadad (KSC / LASSO Microbiologist):** First author of the *Frontiers in Plant Science* synthesis (`PMC7067979`); leads the microbiological food-safety clearance and nutritional/antioxidant profiling across all three Veggie harvests.

- **Mary Hummerick, LaShelle Spencer & Anirudha Dixit (KSC Crop & Bioinformatics Team):** Co-authors driving heterotrophic plating, `Illumina MiSeq` `16S`/`ITS` community sequencing, `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES elemental digestion, and `ASE 350` phytochemical extractions alongside **Jeffrey Richards**, **Matthew Romeyn**, **Trent Smith**, and **Raymond Wheeler**.

- **The Orbital Harvesters (Steve Swanson, Scott Kelly, Kjell Lindgren, Shane Kimbrough):** ISS crew members who tend the `6` rooting pillows, thin seedlings at Day `7`, execute sterile scissor harvests, consume half of `VEG-01B` and `VEG-03A`'s sequential cuts, and pack the foil-wrapped return leaves at `-80°C`.

- **The `'Outredgeous'` Red Romaine Canopy:** *Lactuca sativa* cv. `'Outredgeous'`—carrying anthocyanins, phenolics, and mineral nutrients across `VEG-01A`, `VEG-01B`, and the multi-week "cut-and-come-again" ordeal of `VEG-03A`.

- **The Phyllosphere & Rhizosphere Consortia:** Non-pathogenic leaf-surface bacteria (`2.14–4.86 log₁₀ CFU/g`, zero *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, or *S. aureus*) and root-pillow Proteobacteria (`Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, `Janthinobacterium`) and Ascomycota (`Microidium`, `Alternaria`, `Phaeoacremonium`).

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Before the First Bite (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Full-width orbital shot):** Sunlight rakes across the International Space Station's `Columbus` module. Inside, a soft magenta glow leaks through the bellows of the **Vegetable Production System (Veggie)**.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up):** Six heat-sealed, gas-impermeable `Tedlar` bags open inside the crew work area, revealing six flat rooting pillows packed with porous `Turface Proleague` arcillite and `Nutricote 18-6-8` controlled-release fertilizer.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *May 8, 2014. `SpaceX-3` has docked. Before an astronaut can legally swallow a single leaf grown in microgravity, NASA has to prove the salad won't make them sick.*

- **Panel 3 (Detail):** Two surface-sanitized `'Outredgeous'` seeds sit glued with guar gum between paired germination wicks inside each pillow. A syringe injects `25 mL` of water into the wick.

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1 (Two-shot, KSC SSPF):** Gioia Massa and Christina Khodadad watch the telemetry link from `ISS-Columbus` inside the Kennedy Space Center control room.

- **Gioia Massa:** "`VEG-01A` is live on orbit. `30.5` to `31.75` centimeters below the LEDs—`200 µmol/m²/s` PAR, `12` red, `3` blue, `1` green, `16` hours on, `8` off."

- **Panel 2 (Control chamber inset):** Twenty-four hours behind orbit, a parallel ground-control Veggie unit hums inside a KSC environmental chamber, replaying the ISS temperature (`~23.25°C`) and humidity curve.

- **Christina Khodadad:** "Twenty-four-hour lag for `VEG-01A` and `01B`. Seventy-two hours for `VEG-03A`. Every leaf they freeze upstairs gets a twin on Earth."

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1 (Day 7 montage):** In microgravity, Steve Swanson uses fine forceps to thin each pillow to a single `'Outredgeous'` seedling.

- **Panel 2 (Day 33, `VEG-01A`):** June 10, 2014. Sanitized scissors snip the mature `33`-day leaves. Every leaf is wrapped in aluminum foil and sealed inside the `-80°C` orbital freezer—none eaten yet.

- **Panel 3 (Wide KSC bench):** July 8 – August 10, 2015: **`VEG-01B`** blooms in orbit under Scott Kelly and Kjell Lindgren. Down on Earth, a `NIKON D4S` (`105 mm`, `f/14`) documents the ground-control pillows day by day (`LSDS-109` photography).

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1 (Iconic orbital beat):** August 10, 2015. Scott Kelly and Kjell Lindgren float beside the `VEG-01B` harvest, wiping `'Outredgeous'` leaves with food-safe sanitizing wipes before tasting the first NASA-grown space crop—while the remaining leaves head to `-80°C` for Khodadad's lab.

- **Panel 2 (Timeline jump):** October 25 – December 28, 2016 (`SpaceX-8` era): **`VEG-03A`**. Shane Kimbrough tends the pillows not for a single `33`-day clear-cut, but for **cut-and-come-again** sequential harvesting.

- **Shane Kimbrough:** "First cut at Day `33`, then three more weekly harvests. We eat the first, third, and half the fourth—and send the second harvest plus the rest of the fourth home frozen."

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1 (Wide KSC lab):** Freezer boxes from `VEG-01A`, `VEG-01B`, and `VEG-03A` (`n = 60` leaf samples in `OSD-745`, plus root pillows) arrive at KSC. Christina Khodadad and Mary Hummerick pull on nitrile gloves.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up, agar plates):** Leaf and root homogenates hit heterotrophic plate count media for bacteria, yeast, and mold—alongside selective pathogen screens for *Escherichia coli*, *Salmonella* sp., and *Staphylococcus aureus*.

- **Mary Hummerick:** "First gate is food safety. If *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, or *S. aureus* shows up on those leaves, the whole program pauses."

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1 (Plate counts readout):** Colony counters click across `VEG-01A`, `VEG-01B`, and `VEG-03A` harvests: leaf bacterial counts average **`3.53`**, **`4.86`**, **`2.89`**, and **`2.14 log₁₀ CFU/g`**; fungal counts sit between **`2.3`** and **`4.3 log₁₀ CFU/g`**.

- **Panel 2 (Negative screens):** Every selective pathogen plate—*E. coli*, *Salmonella*, *S. aureus*—comes back **completely negative**, corroborated by `Illumina MiSeq` `16S`/`ITS` amplicon sequencing.

- **Christina Khodadad:** "Lower bacterial loads than typical farm or market produce—and zero target human pathogens."

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor: *The Dual Ledger — Orbit vs. Earth*)**

- **Left Page (Page 7) — *The Living Canopy (`16S` & `ITS` Microbiome)*:** A split botanical silhouette of `'Outredgeous'`—roots anchored in porous arcillite below, ruffled burgundy-green leaves unfurling above. `80–96%` Proteobacteria (`Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, `Janthinobacterium`), `Chitinophaga`, and `Thermogemmatispora` populate the root zone (`10⁶–10⁸ CFU/g`) with far higher Shannon diversity than the leaves, while `Ascomycota` (`92–99%`: `Microidium`, `Alternaria`, `Phaeoacremonium`) dominate the fungi. Only `VEG-03A` shows a significant flight-vs-ground shift in leaf bacterial genera.

- **Right Page (Page 8) — *The Nutritional Assay (`OSD-745`)*:** Freeze-dried `'Outredgeous'` leaf powder feeds four parallel analytical lines: the `Dionex ASE 350` (`1500 psi`, `80–100°C`), the `Beckman DU 700` spectrophotometer (`530`/`650 nm`), the `BioTek Synergy Hybrid` microplate reader (`Folin-Ciocalteu` & `ORAC-FL`), and the `Mod Block` + `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES plasma torch.

- **Spread Caption:** *Safe to swallow is only half the bar. If microgravity strips the minerals or antioxidants out of the leaf, a fresh salad is just crunchy water.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1 (Detail, `ASE 350` cell):** LaShelle Spencer packs `100 mg` of dry leaf powder into an `ASE 350` extraction cell for anthocyanins (`MWA` `85:14.5:0.5`, `100°C`, `1500 psi`, `5 min` static), while `25 mg` aliquots enter parallel cells for phenolics and `ORAC` (`AWA` `70:29.5:0.5`, `80°C`, `1500 psi`).

- **Panel 2 (Spectrophotometer readout):** `Beckman DU 700` measures absorbance at `530` and `650 nm` against a **Cyanidin-3-Glucoside** standard curve.

- **Panel 3 (Result):** Across `VEG-01A`, `VEG-01B`, and `VEG-03A`, flight and ground anthocyanin levels show **no significant difference**.

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1 (Microplate setup):** On the `BioTek Synergy Hybrid` reader (`37°C`, `2 h` decay), `20 µL` of `1/50`-diluted `AWA` extract meets `200 µL` fluorescein and `20 µL` `AAPH` peroxyl radical generator in a forward-then-reverse `96`-well layout (edge wells skipped to block plate effects), calibrated to **Trolox** equivalents (`µmol TE/g` DW).

- **Panel 2 (Curve overlay):** Decay curves for flight and ground leaves overlap tightly.

- **LaShelle Spencer:** "ORAC antioxidant capacity didn't budge either. Spaceflight didn't dull the radical-scavenging power."

### Act II: The Phenolic Dip & The Elemental Ledger (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1 (Colorimetric tubes):** `0.2 mL` aliquots react with **Folin-Ciocalteu** phenol reagent against a **gallic acid (GA)** calibration curve (`BioTek Synergy Hybrid`).

- **Panel 2 (Bar chart):** `VEG-01A` and `VEG-01B` hold high total phenolics—but **`VEG-03A`** drops significantly (`p ≤ 0.001`), averaging **`15.0 mg/g` DW (ground)** and **`19.6 mg/g` DW (flight)**.

- **Christina Khodadad:** "Repeated weekly clipping in `VEG-03A`—or its longer `56`-day run—changed the phenolic baseline across the crop."

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1 (Acid digestion hood):** `0.2–0.5 g` of dried, ground leaf tissue sits in `5 mL` of `70%` trace-metal-grade `HNO₃` on a `95°C` graphite `Mod Block` (EPA Method 3050B mod.), boiling clear for `2 h` before `2.5 mL` `30% H₂O₂` foams and clears, then filtering through `0.45 µm` into `50 mL` ultra-pure DI water.

- **Panel 2 (`iCAP 7000` ICP-OES):** Sample mist hits the argon plasma.

- **Panel 3 (Two-shot):** Jeffrey Richards and Matthew Romeyn scan the elemental table.

- **Jeffrey Richards:** "Within any single planting, flight and ground match. No microgravity mineral penalty."

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1 (Cross-experiment comparison chart):** Comparing *across* the three plantings, the `iCAP 7000` reveals sharp inter-mission shifts: **`Fe`** (`p ≤ 0.001`) and **`K`** (`p ≤ 0.0001`) are significantly lower in `VEG-03A` than in `VEG-01A` or `VEG-01B`.

- **Panel 2 (Second chart):** Meanwhile, **`VEG-01B`** spikes higher in **`Na`** (`p ≤ 0.0001`), **`P`** (`p ≤ 0.05`), **`S`** (`p ≤ 0.05`), and **`Zn`** (`p ≤ 0.0001`), while **`Ca`**, **`Mg`**, and **`Mn`** stay flat across all three tests.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "Hardware watering, pillow blend (`100%` `600 µm–1 mm` vs. `1:1` `1–2 mm`), and harvest schedule drive more mineral variance than microgravity itself."

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1 (Microbial detective work):** Anirudha Dixit pulls up the `Illumina MiSeq` (`V2 500-cycle`) taxonomic bars (`PMC7067979` Figure 4).

- **Panel 2 (Comparison):** In `VEG-01A` and `VEG-01B`, `80–96%` of bacterial reads are Proteobacteria (`Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, `Janthinobacterium`), with `Chitinophaga` higher in flight roots (except `VEG-01B` ground).

- **Panel 3 (Highlight on `VEG-03A`):** In `VEG-03A`, nitrogen-fixing `Azospirillum` and `Herbaspirillum` rise, `Thermogemmatispora` drops, and—for the first time—**flight vs. ground leaf bacterial genera diverge significantly**.

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1 (Fungal bar chart):** `Ascomycota` accounts for `92–99%` of fungal reads; `Basidiomycota` hits `7%` in `VEG-01A` flight roots and `6%` in `VEG-01B` flight roots (`≤2%` elsewhere).

- **Panel 2 (Microscopic silhouettes):** Obligate biotroph `Microidium` dominates leaves alongside `Alternaria`, `Malassezia`, and `Fusarium` (`VEG-01B` only), while roots harbor `Alternaria`, `Phaeoacremonium`, and `Rhodosporidiobolus`, and culturable `Rhodotorula` appears in almost every sample except `VEG-03A` leaves.

- **Mary Hummerick:** "Root diversity is always richer than leaf diversity—and every culturable isolate showed up in the sequencing too."

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1 (Wide KSC conference room):** The full Veggie team—Massa, Khodadad, Hummerick, Spencer, Dixit, Richards, Romeyn, Smith, Wheeler—reviews the integrated `VEG-01A`/`01B`/`03A` verdict.

- **Panel 2 (Checklist):**

  - Human pathogens: **0**

  - Leaf CFU counts: **Low (`2.14–4.86 log₁₀ CFU/g`)**

  - Anthocyanins & ORAC: **Maintained in space**

  - Flight vs. Ground minerals: **Equivalent within each mission**

- **Gioia Massa:** "Veggie works. Astronauts can grow and eat `'Outredgeous'` on the ISS safely, repeatedly, and with full antioxidant value."

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1 (Data curation terminal):** Years after the 2020 paper, the `OSD-745` (`LSDS-109`) dataset is standardized by the **ALSDA Analysis Working Group** into machine-readable row/column templates—linking `60` leaf samples, `NIKON D4S` photography, `Beckman DU 700` anthocyanins, `BioTek` phenolics & `ORAC`, and `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES elements under `DOI: 10.26030/4tsr-7518`.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up):** `OSD-745` goes live on NASA OSDR (`22-Dec-2025`), completing the analytical loop with `OSD-267`, `OSD-268`, and `OSD-269`.

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1 (Reflective beat):** Christina Khodadad looks at a printed photo of Scott Kelly holding a red romaine leaf in `Columbus`.

- **Christina Khodadad:** "Salads are morale and micronutrients. They're not calories."

- **Panel 2 (Wide shot):** Beyond the SSPF windows, the Space Coast sky fades to indigo. On a nearby whiteboard, Artemis lunar-surface mission timelines replace ISS orbital tracks.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "On the Moon, nobody's shipping `25`-milliliter arcillite pillows for every meal. You need starch. You need tubers. You need **local dirt**."

### Act III: From Orbital Salad to Lunar Dust (Pages 19–30)

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1 (Transition):** A conceptual diagram unfolds: ISS **Veggie** (`200 µmol/m²/s`, `Nutricote` + `Turface` arcillite, `33–56` days) sits on the left; on the right, a lunar habitat module rests in grey **regolith**.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *Lettuce proved that spaceflight crops can be safe and nutritious. Now the frontier shifts from microgravity greenhouses to planetary surfaces—and to the staple crop built for high harvest index.*

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1 (Close-up):** A sprouted seed tuber of **potato** (*Solanum tuberosum*) rests beside five dark glass jars of crushed volcanic rock and anorthosite: **Lunar Regolith Simulants (LRS)**.

- **Panel 2 (Labels on the jars):** Two lunar **mare** simulants (including `LMS-1E`) and three lunar **highland** simulants (including `LHS-1E`, `NUW-LHT-5M`, `OPRH4W30`)—plus `JSC-1A` and **vermicompost** (worm castings) at `0%`, `15%`, and `30%`.

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1 (Lab bench):** At Oregon State University, a `PlantEye` multispectral `3D` scanner sweeps over emerging potato shoots while a handheld `PhotosynQ MultispeQ` clamps onto a leaf to log chlorophyll fluorescence, electrochromic shift (`ECS`), and `P700` absorbance.

- **Panel 2 (Alert readout):** Plant size shrinks in bare lunar regolith simulant compared to control soil. `Mehlich-3` bio-extractable ICP-OES (`Agilent 5110`) flashes a warning: **copper (`Cu`) overaccumulation** and hostile substrate `pH`/`EC`.

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1 (Molecular readout):** `Illumina NovaSeq X Plus` RNA-seq (`OS-927`) lights up differentially expressed genes tied to **stress response** and the **chloroplast**, while `GC-MS` metabolite profiling (`Fiehn` library, ribitol-normalized) flags shifting **fructose** and tuber metabolites.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *The first ISS lettuce harvest answered whether space food is safe. Lunar potato asks whether we can farm the Moon itself.*

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1 (Comparison panel):** Back at KSC, Gioia Massa files the final `OSD-745` (`LSDS-109`) release checklist—connecting `VEG-01A` (`2014`), `VEG-01B` (`2015`), and `VEG-03A` (`2016`) into one open-access baseline.

- **Panel 2 (Detail):** Five assay icons lock into place: `Image Analysis`, `ICP-OES`, `ORAC`, `Phenolics`, `Anthocyanins`.

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1 (Medium shot):** LaShelle Spencer closes the `OSD-745` archive folder—bridging her earlier `Ag⁺` hydroponics warning (`OSD-723`) with the Veggie arcillite baseline that made ISS harvests possible in the first place.

- **LaShelle Spencer:** "Arcillite protected `'Outredgeous'` on the station. Now let's see what happens when the substrate isn't sterile clay—it's Moon dust and worm castings."

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1 (Montage):** A `VEG-03A` leaf in `-80°C` foil; a `Mod Block` acid digest boiling clear; a `BioTek` fluorometer tracing `2`-hour `ORAC` decay; a `NIKON D4S` shutter snapping at `1/100 s`.

- **Panel 2 (Quiet beat):** All `60` samples of `OSD-745` settle into the OSDR vault (`138.01 MB`, `CC0-1.0`).

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1 (Visual bridge):** A red romaine leaf dissolves into a cross-section of a swelling **potato tuber** beneath grey lunar basalt grains.

- **Panel 2 (Environmental shift):** `101 kPa` ISS cabin air gives way to a `63`-day lunar-simulant pot trial; `Nutricote` pellets give way to `5%`, `15%`, and `30%` vermicompost amendments.

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1 (Close-up, `LMS-1E` vs. `LHS-1E`):** Sharp, unweathered mare and highland mineral shards surround a young *Solanum tuberosum* root—leaching trace metals and starving the rhizosphere of organic structure until worm-castings compost softens the blow.

- **Panel 2 (Scan beam):** The `PlantEye` laser line sweeps across the canopy at `0`, `8`, `24`, and `63` days after planting.

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1 (Data cascade):** `MultispeQ` `NPQ` and quantum-yield curves, `Agilent 5110` `Mehlich-3` `Al/Ca/Cu/Fe/K/Mg/Mn/P/Zn` bars, `GC-MS` `ribitol`-normalized peaks, and `NovaSeq X Plus` chloroplast transcripts converge on screen.

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Double-Page Spread: *Next Station — `OSD-750`*)**

- **Left Page (Page 29):** High above the lunar South Pole, a pressurized dome glows against the regolith horizon. Inside, rows of green *Solanum tuberosum* canopies rise from dark, compost-amended lunar mare and highland simulants.

- **Right Page (Page 30):** Split-frame analytical preview of **`OSD-750`** (`GLDS-667` / `LSDS-165`): five lunar regolith simulants (`LMS-1E`, `LHS-1E`, `JSC-1A`, `NUW-LHT-5M`, `OPRH4W30`), `Cu` toxicity warnings, chloroplast RNA-seq DEGs, and `GC-MS` fructose shifts.

- **Spread Caption:** *We proved astronauts can eat fresh greens in orbit. Now, to stay on the Moon, we have to teach a potato to survive regolith.*

- **Cliffhanger Tag:** **NEXT VOLUME: `OSD-750` — *Effects of Lunar Regolith Simulant on Potato Growth, Nutrition, and Gene Expression*.**

## 4. Mission Debrief (Pages 31–32 Infographic Layout)

### Left Spread — Page 31: ISS Veggie Flight & Assay Architecture (`OSD-745` / `LSDS-109`)

| Payload / Mission | Growth Schedule & Harvest Mode | Ground Control Lag & Lighting | Analytical Assays in `OSD-745` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **`VEG-01A`** (`SpaceX-3`) | `May 8–Jun 10, 2014` (`33` days; single final harvest, all frozen) | `24 h` delay; `~200 µmol/m²/s` (`12:3:1` R:B:G, `16:8` L:D) | Anthocyanins, Phenolics, `ORAC`, `iCAP 7000` ICP-OES |
| **`VEG-01B`** (ISS) | `Jul 8–Aug 10, 2015` (`33` days; first crew-consumed harvest + frozen return) | `24 h` delay; `23.25°C`, `6` arcillite/`Nutricote` pillows | `NIKON D4S` photography + full phytochemical/ICP-OES suite |
| **`VEG-03A`** (`SpaceX-8` era) | `Oct 25–Dec 28, 2016` (`33` days + `3` weekly cut-and-come-again harvests) | `72 h` delay; `1st`, `3rd`, half `4th` eaten; `2nd` + half `4th` returned | Same `4` chemical/elemental assays (`n = 60` total samples) |

### Right Spread — Page 32: Nutritional, Antioxidant & Food-Safety Outcomes (`OSD-745` + `PMC7067979`)

| Assay / Metric | Flight vs. Ground Outcome | Cross-Experiment (`VEG-01A`/`01B`/`03A`) Pattern | Crew Food-Safety & Nutrition Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Anthocyanins & `ORAC-FL`** | No significant difference (`Beckman DU 700` / `BioTek`) | No significant difference across all `3` plantings | Spaceflight preserves `'Outredgeous'` antioxidant capacity |
| **Total Phenolics** (`GAE`) | Equivalent within each mission | `VEG-03A` lowest (`15.0` ground, `19.6` flight `mg/g` DW; `p ≤ 0.001`) | Sequential clipping/age alters phenolics more than flight |
| **ICP-OES Elements** (`iCAP 7000`) | No flight-vs-ground difference within any test | `VEG-03A` lower `Fe`, `K`; `VEG-01B` higher `Na`, `P`, `S`, `Zn`; `Ca/Mg/Mn` flat | Mineral profiles stay safe and mission-dependent |
| **Microbial Counts & Pathogens** | `2.14–4.86 log₁₀ CFU/g` bacteria; `2.3–4.3` fungi; `VEG-03A` leaf genera differed | `Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, `Janthinobacterium`, `Ascomycota` (`92–99%`); zero *E. coli*/*Salmonella*/*S. aureus* | Microbiologically safe fresh food supplement for ISS crew |

## 1. Volume Metadata Header

- **Series:** *Roots in Orbit: The NASA OSDR Plant Chronicles*

- **Volume:** 59

- **Chapter Title:** *Tubers in the Basalt Dust*

- **OSDR Accession:** `OSD-750` (`GeneLab ID: GLDS-667` | `ALSDA ID: LSDS-165`, Version 1 | `DOI: 10.26030/w56j-2d69` | License: `CC0-1.0` | Size: `56.54 GB` | Submitted: `08-Jul-2024` | Initial Release: `18-Nov-2026`)

- **Project & Primary Team:** NASA Project `OS-927` (*Growth, physiology and nutrition dynamics of potato plants grown on lunar regolith simulant medium*, Grant `# 80NSSC24K0755`); Aymeric Goyer & David Handy (Oregon State University), with Anika Loeffler, Sydney Campbell, and Medora Knudson (associated `Goyer2026` supplementary data tables curated in OSDR).

- **Skipped Accessions:** `OSD-746` through `OSD-749` (contain no plant studies)

- **Hardware & Environment:** Oregon State University greenhouse (`22°C` day / `18°C` night, `20°C` mean, natural sunlight); `8.89 × 7.62 cm` square pots (`~300 mL` substrate) lined with landscaping fabric; `Osmocote Plus 15-9-12` (`43 cm³` per `7,570 cm³`); `40 mL` RO water every `2–3` days increasing to daily; **Exp. 1:** Lunar Mare Simulant `LMS-1E` vs. Oregon `Adkins` sandy soil (`0%`, `15%`, `30% v/v` vermicompost); **Exp. 2:** `Adkins` soil vs. five LRSs (`JSC-1A`, `LMS-1E` mare; `LHS-1E`, `NUW-LHT-5M`, `OPRH4W30` highland) each with `5%` vermicompost.

- **Organism & Assay Scope:** *Solanum tuberosum* cv. `'Modoc'` mini-tubers (`n = 173` total samples in OSDR; `74 DAP` harvest in Exp. 1, `59 DAP` in Exp. 2); **3D Multispectral Imaging** (`Phenospex PlantEye F600`), **Chlorophyll Fluorescence** (`PhotosynQ MultispeQ`), **Biomass**, **Substrate Chemistry** (`Hanna HI5522` `pH`/`EC`, `Picarro` `CO₂` burst, `Agilent 5110` ICP-OES), **RNA-Seq** (`Illumina NovaSeq X Plus` `2 × 150 bp`, `39 DAP` leaf), and **GC-MS Metabolomics** (`Agilent 7890B-5977B`, `Fiehn 2013` library, `39 DAP` leaf & `59 DAP` tuber).

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **Dr. Aymeric Goyer (Oregon State University Principal Investigator):** Conceptualizer of `OS-927`; tests whether potato—a high-harvest-index staple tuber crop—can survive and yield in lunar mare and highland regolith simulants amended with worm castings.

- **David Handy (Oregon State University Investigation Lead):** Oversees the two greenhouse trials (`2024` compost-ratio screen and `2025` five-simulant comparison), `PlantEye F600` `3D` point-cloud scans, `MultispeQ` leaf-clamp physiology, and `74`-/`59`-day tuber harvests.

- **Anika Loeffler, Sydney Campbell & Medora Knudson (OSU Undergraduate & Beginning Researchers):** Support plant care, `Virtis` freeze-drying, mortar-and-pestle grinding, and soil/metabolite sample preparation.

- **The `'Modoc'` Mini-Tubers (*Solanum tuberosum*):** Sprouted to `2 cm` and planted into `300 mL` pots—forced to push stolons and swell daughter tubers inside crushed silicate rock rather than Earth loam.

- **The Five Lunar Simulants (`LMS-1E`, `JSC-1A`, `LHS-1E`, `NUW-LHT-5M`, `OPRH4W30`):** Two dark basaltic mare simulants and three pale anorthositic highland simulants—low in organic carbon (`CO₂` burst `1–2 µg/g/day` unamended), alkaline at start (`pH 7.9`), and prone to releasing excess bio-available copper (`Cu`).

- **The Vermicompost Microbiome (`5%` Non-Autoclaved + `0–25%` Autoclaved):** Worm castings blended at `0%`, `5%`, `15%`, or `30% (v/v)` to equalize the starting microbial inoculum while buffering `pH`, raising `CO₂` respiration (`25 µg/g/day` at `30%`), and supplying organic structure.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Planting the Moon (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Full-width establishing shot):** Morning sunlight slants across the Oregon State University greenhouse benches. Rows of `8.89 × 7.62 cm` square pots sit beneath the gantry of a **Phenospex `PlantEye F600`** `3D` laser scanner.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up):** A gloved hand lines each pot with dark landscaping fabric and spoons in `300 mL` of slate-grey **Lunar Mare Simulant `LMS-1E`** mixed with `Osmocote Plus 15-9-12`.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *Lettuce in orbit gave astronauts fresh vitamins. To live on the Moon, they need calories—and nothing packs starch per square meter like potato.*

- **Panel 3 (Two-shot):** Aymeric Goyer and David Handy check the sprouted `'Modoc'` mini-tubers (`CSS Farms`) resting beside buckets of dark vermicompost.

- **Aymeric Goyer:** "We can't haul Iowa topsoil to Shackleton Crater. If we want lunar tubers, we have to see what `'Modoc'` does in crushed mare and highland rock."

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1 (Map & soil sample inset):** Reference control: **Adkins-series sandy soil** dug from the top `30 cm` of an uncultivated ryegrass field in Umatilla County, Oregon (`45.817318, -119.294922`).

- **Panel 2 (Experiment 1 matrix, August 2, 2024):** Six treatments (`n = 36` pots): `100%`, `85%`, and `70%` `LMS-1E` vs. `100%`, `85%`, and `70%` `Adkins` soil—blended with **`0%`**, **`15%`**, or **`30%` vermicompost**.

- **David Handy:** "Every amended pot gets `5%` non-autoclaved worm castings plus `10%` or `25%` autoclaved castings—so `15%` and `30%` start with the exact same living microbiome."

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1 (Baseline soil lab readout):** At the OSU Soil Health Lab, a `Hanna HI5522` probe dips into `1:1` substrate-water slurries, while a `Picarro` isotopic `CO₂` analyzer tracks `24 h` and `96 h` respiration at `23°C`.

- **Panel 2 (Numbers on screen):** Pure `LMS-1E` (`0%` compost) reads **`pH 7.9`**, **`EC 0.73 dS/m`**, and a near-sterile **`2 µg CO₂-C/g/day`** at `24 h`. At `30%` vermicompost, `LMS-1E` drops to **`pH 7.06`**, **`EC 2.03 dS/m`**, and jumps twelve-fold to **`25 µg CO₂-C/g/day`**.

- **Panel 3 (Action):** `40 mL` of reverse-osmosis water wets each pot as greenhouse vents hold `22°C` day / `18°C` night.

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1 (Overhead scanner pass, Days 20–33):** Every `12` hours, the `PlantEye F600` sweeps overhead—triangulating `3D` laser point clouds and logging red, green, blue, and near-infrared reflectance (`29` scans per plant).

- **Panel 2 (Digital readout):** Point clouds resolve into digital biomass (`height × 3D leaf area`), leaf angle, `NDVI`, `NPCI`, and `PSRI` senescence index.

- **Anika Loeffler:** "In pure `LMS-1E` (`0%` compost), emergence is patchy—only `4` of `6` tubers even break the surface, and the canopies stay compact."

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1 (Day 63, October 4, 2024):** Sydney Campbell clamps a handheld **`PhotosynQ MultispeQ`** onto light-adapted `'Modoc'` leaves (`22` plants, `3` readings each).

- **Panel 2 (Instrument screen):** `Phi2` (`PhiPSII`), `PhiNPQ`, `NPQt`, linear electron flow (`LEF`), electrochromic shift (`ECS tau`), proton conductivity (`gH+`), `SPAD` chlorophyll, and `PS1` redox centers stream to the tablet.

- **Aymeric Goyer:** "Even when the leaves look green, the `MultispeQ` catches how hard the photosystems are working to dump excess light energy."

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1 (Day 74 Harvest, October 15, 2024):** Pots tip onto stainless sieves. Shoots, roots, and daughter tubers are rinsed free of `LMS-1E` grit and weighed fresh (`shoot:root` ratio and `harvest index = 100 × tuber / [tuber + shoot]`).

- **Panel 2 (Freeze-dryer):** Leaves and tubers flash-freeze in liquid nitrogen and enter a `Virtis Benchtop 4.0K XL` lyophilizer for `48` hours, while post-growth `LMS-1E` (`pH` down to `5.18–6.39`) goes to `Anton Paar` microwave `HNO₃` digestion and `Agilent 5110` ICP-OES.

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor: *Five Faces of the Moon*)**

- **Left Page (Page 7) — *Experiment 2: The Five-Simulant Gauntlet (May 5, 2025)*:** Five lunar regolith simulants line the greenhouse bench alongside `Adkins` soil, each softened with **`5% (v/v)` vermicompost** (`n = 30`): dark basaltic **`JSC-1A`** and **`LMS-1E`** (mare), and pale feldspathic **`LHS-1E`**, **`NUW-LHT-5M`**, and **`OPRH4W30`** (highland).

- **Right Page (Page 8) — *The `35`-Day `PlantEye` Time-Lapse (`70` Scans/Plant)*:** By Day `8`, shoots pierce `Adkins`, `JSC-1A`, `LMS-1E`, `LHS-1E`, and `OPRH4W30`—yet **`NUW-LHT-5M`** remains barren grey dust until Day `24`, finally pushing up a dwarfed, struggling sprout while `Adkins` towers beside it.

- **Spread Caption:** *Mare basalt and highland anorthosite are not the same Moon. Put a potato in five lunar simulants, and one of them barely lets the shoot breathe.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1 (Day 39 Sampling, Exp. 2):** Medora Knudson snips upper-canopy leaves—before senescence sets in—and plunges them straight into liquid nitrogen for **RNA-seq** and **GC-MS** metabolomics.

- **Panel 2 (Empty tube):** At the `NUW-LHT-5M` pots, her forceps pause. The plants are so severely stunted there isn't enough leaf tissue to sample without destroying the experiment.

- **David Handy:** "`NUW-LHT-5M` skips `39`-day leaf RNA-seq altogether. We'll see what's left at tuber harvest."

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1 (Day 59 Harvest, July 3, 2025):** Final tuber weights are logged across the five simulants and `Adkins` control, and post-growth substrates from four replicates per treatment head to `Mehlich-3` extraction (`20 mL` per `2 g`, `5 min` shake) and `Agilent 5110` ICP-OES (`Al, Ca, Cu, Fe, K, Mg, Mn, P, Zn`).

- **Panel 2 (Alert flag on ICP-OES):** One micronutrient bar spikes sharply above the `Adkins` baseline: **copper (`Cu`)**.

- **Aymeric Goyer:** "That's the suspect. Bio-available copper leaching out of crushed lunar rock."

### Act II: Chloroplast Stress & The Fructose Shift (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1 (Molecular bench):** Frozen `39 DAP` leaves from `Adkins`, `JSC-1A`, `LMS-1E`, `LHS-1E`, and `OPRH4W30` undergo `Purelink` RNA extraction and `Agilent Bioanalyzer 2100` QC.

- **Panel 2 (Sequencing cluster):** Libraries stream off an **`Illumina NovaSeq X Plus`** (`150 bp` paired-end, `20.8–28.8 million` reads per sample), checked with `fastq_utils v0.25.1`, `FastQC v0.11.9`, and `MultiQC v1.12`.

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1 (Transcriptome volcano/pathway view):** Differential expression lights up two dominant hubs in LRS-grown `'Modoc'` leaves compared with `Adkins` soil: **stress-response genes** and **chloroplast-localized transcripts**.

- **Panel 2 (Cellular cross-section):** Inside a mesophyll cell, excess `Cu` and alkaline/mineral stress press against the thylakoid membrane—triggering chloroplast redox remodeling and `NPQ` photoprotection.

- **Aymeric Goyer:** "Even when a potato survives in lunar regolith simulant, its chloroplasts are rewriting their playbook to cope."

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1 (Metabolomics prep):** `50 mg` of lyophilized leaf and tuber powder drops into `water:methanol:chloroform (1:2.5:1)` spiked with **`40 µg/mL` ribitol** as an internal standard.

- **Panel 2 (Derivatization):** Dried aqueous extracts react with `20 µL` methoxyamine hydrochloride (`90 min`, `37°C`) and `40 µL` `MSTFA + 1% TMCS` (`30 min`, `37°C`), then inject (`1 µL`, `10:1` leaf / `4:1` tuber split) into an **`Agilent 7890B-5977B` GC-MS**.

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1 (Chromatogram peaks):** Spectra match against the `Agilent Fiehn 2013` RTL library in `AMDIS` and normalize to `ribitol` in `MetaboAnalyst 6.0`.

- **Panel 2 (Highlighted peak):** **Fructose**—alongside other central carbon and stress metabolites—accumulates differentially between LRS-grown plants and `Adkins` controls.

- **David Handy:** "Smaller canopies, stressed chloroplasts, and altered sugar partitioning straight into the tubers."

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1 (Comparison panel — Exp. 1 vs. Exp. 2):** Side-by-side summary of the two experiments:

  - **Compost rescue (Exp. 1):** Blending `15%` or `30%` vermicompost into `LMS-1E` buffers `pH` (`7.9` → `7.06` pre-growth), boosts `CO₂` respiration (`2` → `25 µg/g/day`), and supports canopy & tuber set.

  - **Simulant divergence (Exp. 2):** With only `5%` vermicompost, all LRSs trail `Adkins` soil in plant size—and highland `NUW-LHT-5M` stalls almost completely.

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1 (Detail, `Mehlich-3` vs. `HNO₃`):** An analytical note reminds the team: Experiment 1's microwave `HNO₃` digestion measures *total* rock metals (`Al, Cr, Cu, Fe, Ni, Zn`), while Experiment 2's `Mehlich-3` measures the *bio-extractable* fraction roots actually taste.

- **Panel 2 (Two-shot):** Aymeric Goyer and David Handy review the `OS-927` (`OSD-750`) dataset—`56.54 GB` of `PlantEye` point-cloud stats, `MultispeQ` fluorescence, `GC-MS` peak tables, and `NovaSeq X Plus` RNA-seq.

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1 (Curation terminal):** The ALSDA Analysis Working Group aligns `OSD-750` (`GLDS-667` / `LSDS-165`, `DOI: 10.26030/w56j-2d69`) into standardized machine-readable CSVs (`Data1`–`Data9`, `TableS5`–`TableS6`) for public release on `18-Nov-2026`.

- **Panel 2 (Caption):** *The verdict for lunar greenhouses: raw regolith is not soil. Without organic amendment (`15–30%` compost) and micronutrient mitigation (`Cu`), even a hardy tuber like `'Modoc'` pays a steep physiological tax.*

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1 (Quiet greenhouse evening):** The `PlantEye F600` gantry parks at the end of its rail. Empty `NUW-LHT-5M` and `LMS-1E` pots sit beside harvested `'Modoc'` tubers.

- **Aymeric Goyer:** "We've tested leafy greens in Veggie. We've tested tubers in Moon dust. What about the one crop astronauts crave most—something with **heat**, **fruit**, and **color**?"

### Act III: From Lunar Dust to the 137-Day Pepper (Pages 19–30)

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1 (Flashback / Orbit transition):** High above Earth, inside the International Space Station's **Advanced Plant Habitat (`APH`)**, `48` seeds sit glued with guar in four independently controlled ceramic-substrate quadrants (`1–2 mm` autoclaved arcillite + `Nutricote`).

- **Caption (Narrator):** *June 3, 2021. `SpaceX CRS-22` carries `PH-04` to orbit—not a `28`-day salad, not a `74`-day greenhouse tuber, but a `137`-day fruiting marathon.*

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1 (Close-up):** A glowing red-and-green **`Capsicum annuum` cv. `'NuMex Española Improved'`** chile pepper hangs under the `APH` LED canopy—one of `26` pepper fruits harvested in microgravity.

- **Panel 2 (Microbiology link):** Alongside fruit yield and crew taste tests, swab and plant samples enter `16S` `V4` amplicon sequencing on `Illumina MiSeq` (`2 × 250 bp`) using the exact `Khodadad et al., 2020` barcoded primer protocol we saw in `OSD-745`.

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1 (Contrast panel):** Back in Oregon, David Handy packs the last `'Modoc'` tuber sample into `-80°C` storage, glancing at the ISS `APH` telemetry feed.

- **David Handy:** "On the Moon, we're fighting `Cu` and dead rock. In orbit, `APH` had to keep a flowering, fruiting pepper alive for four and a half months."

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1 (Split graphic):**

  - Left: *Solanum tuberosum* `'Modoc'` (`OSD-750`, `59–74` days, `5` lunar simulants, `Cu` stress, chloroplast RNA-seq, `GC-MS` fructose).

  - Right: *Capsicum annuum* `'NuMex Española Improved'` (`OSD-772`, `137` days, `PH-04` / `SpaceX-22`, `26` fruits, `n = 109` samples).

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1 (Soil-health archive):** `OSD-750` locks its `173` sample records into NASA OSDR (`18-Nov-2026`), giving lunar ISRU agricultural engineers the first multi-omic potato baseline across both mare and highland simulants.

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1 (Close-up, `LMS-1E` vs. `Adkins`):** A single `'Modoc'` mini-tuber rests on a clean scale—small, scarred by silicate grit, yet carrying the starch blueprint for future lunar habitats.

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1 (Transition):** The greenhouse glass darkens; the scene dissolves into the sterile stainless interior of the ISS `APH` growth chamber (`137` days on the mission clock).

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1 (Botanical close-up):** White *Capsicum* blossoms open in microgravity—requiring pollination without wind or bees—before swelling into glossy green and crimson chile pods.

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1 (Hardware schematic):** Four `990 g` ceramic-substrate quadrants inside the `APH` Science Carrier, each feeding `12` pepper seeds (`48` total) through `137` continuous days of closed-loop orbital environmental control.

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1 (Crew & Lab link):** `26` pepper fruits harvested in space—part eaten fresh by the ISS crew in orbital tacos, part swabbed and sequenced (`16S` `MiSeq` `2 × 250 bp`) to verify food safety after the longest continuous plant experiment ever run on the station.

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Double-Page Spread: *Next Station — `OSD-772`*)**

- **Left Page (Page 29):** Inside the `Advanced Plant Habitat`, glowing crimson `'NuMex Española Improved'` peppers hang amidst dense green foliage—a burst of fiery color against the orbital night.

- **Right Page (Page 30):** Mission telemetry overlay for **`OSD-772`** (`PH-04 Chile Peppers in Space`, `SpaceX-22`, `137` days, `26` fruits, `48` plants across `4` quadrants, `n = 109` samples, `16S` `MiSeq`).

- **Spread Caption:** *Lunar dust tested how far a staple tuber can bend. Next, we return to the International Space Station for `137` days of patience—and the first chile peppers ever grown in space.*

- **Cliffhanger Tag:** **NEXT VOLUME: `OSD-772` — *PH-04 Chile Peppers in Space*.**

## 4. Mission Debrief (Pages 31–32 Infographic Layout)

### Left Spread — Page 31: Two-Experiment Lunar Simulant Design (`OSD-750` / `GLDS-667`)

| Experiment | Substrates & Amendments | Design & Duration | Phenotyping & Soil Assays |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Exp. 1** (`2024`) | `LMS-1E` (mare) vs. `Adkins` sandy soil + `0%`, `15%`, `30%` vermicompost (`5%` live + `0–25%` autoclaved) | `n = 36` pots (`3–6` emerged/group), `74 DAP` harvest (`15-Oct-2024`) | `PlantEye F600` (`20–33 DAP`, `29` scans), `MultispeQ` (`63 DAP`), fresh biomass, `HNO₃` ICP-OES, `pH`/`EC`/`CO₂` |
| **Exp. 2** (`2025`) | `Adkins` soil vs. `JSC-1A`, `LMS-1E` (mare) & `LHS-1E`, `NUW-LHT-5M`, `OPRH4W30` (highland) + `5%` vermicompost | `n = 30` pots (`5` reps/substrate), `39 DAP` leaf, `59 DAP` tuber (`3-Jul-2025`) | `PlantEye F600` (`0–35 DAP`, `70` scans), `NovaSeq X Plus` RNA-seq, `GC-MS` (`7890B-5977B`), `Mehlich-3` ICP-OES |

### Right Spread — Page 32: Physiological, Transcriptomic & Metabolic Outcomes (`OSD-750`)

| Assay / Domain | Key Observation in LRS vs. `Adkins` Soil | Standout Simulant / Treatment Effect | Lunar Agriculture Takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Plant Size & Emergence** | LRS reduces plant size vs. `Adkins` soil | `NUW-LHT-5M` emergence delayed to `~24 DAP`; too stunted for `39 DAP` leaf RNA-seq | Highland/mare simulants require substantial organic buffering |
| **Substrate Chemistry** | Unamended `LMS-1E` is alkaline (`pH 7.9`) & low-respiration (`2 µg CO₂-C/g/day`) | `30%` vermicompost lowers `pH` (`7.06` → `5.18`), boosts `CO₂` (`25 µg/g/day`); `Cu` overaccumulates | Excess bio-available `Cu` is a candidate driver of LRS stunting |
| **Leaf Transcriptome** (`RNA-Seq`) | `20.8–28.8M` `150 bp` PE reads/sample (`NovaSeq X Plus`) | DEGs enriched in **stress response** and **chloroplast** pathways | LRS triggers photosynthetic & oxidative stress remodeling |
| **Leaf & Tuber Metabolome** (`GC-MS`) | `ribitol`-normalized `Fiehn 2013` / `MetaboAnalyst 6.0` | **Fructose** and other metabolites accumulate differentially in LRS | Carbon partitioning and tuber nutrition shift under LRS stress |

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **Dr. Christina L. M. Khodadad & Dr. Anirudha R. Dixit (Co-Corresponding Authors, Noetic Strategies / AETOS):** Lead the microbial food-safety clearance and `QIIME2`/`DADA2` `16S` community dissection across `Q1–Q4` tissues, swabs, foam, wicks, and water.

- **Dr. Gioia D. Massa, Matthew W. Romeyn & Jacob J. Torres (KSC & NMSU `PH-04` Architects):** Conceptualize `PH-04` and down-select `'NuMex Española Improved'` (a Hatch Big Jim × Española cross) from over two dozen pepper cultivars—guided by Torres, an Española, New Mexico native.

- **Mary Hummerick, LaShelle Spencer, Oscar Monje, Lucie Poulet, Nicole DuFour, Jeffrey Richards, Cory Spern, Jennifer Gooden, Aaron Curry & Raymond Wheeler:** The KSC/Redwire/Sierra Space tele-operations, horticulture, and analytical team tuning `40%` blue light, `550 ppm` CO₂, and `APH` moisture for `137` days from Earth.

- **The Orbital Pollination & Harvest Crew (Megan McArthur, Mark Vande Hei, Shane Kimbrough, Kayla Barron, Thomas Pesquet):** Tend the `4` pepper plants in `Kibo`—thinning at Day `28`, installing support stands at Day `50`, hand-pollinating blossoms, and turning half the `26`-fruit harvest into orbital space tacos.

- **The `'NuMex Española Improved'` Plants (`Q1–Q4`):** Four independently watered root zones (`990 g` arcillite each) kept compact (`< 40 cm`) by `40%` blue light while enduring `137` days of closed-loop microgravity.

- **The `14`-Taxon Core & ISS Water Guild (`Sphingomonas`, `Novosphingobium`, `Pseudomonas`, `Puia`, `Cupriavidus`, `Burkholderia`):** Microbes traced across sanitized seeds, `Q1–Q4` roots, stems, fruits, and `SC` hardware—proving vertical/horizontal niche exchange while leaving the edible peppers pathogen-free.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Forty Percent Blue (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Full-width establishing shot):** Inside the `Kibo` module of the International Space Station, the **Advanced Plant Habitat (`APH`)** hums quietly—an enclosed, `180+`-sensor climate vault built for crops that take months, not weeks.

- **Panel 2 (Close-up, April 2021 at KSC):** Gloved hands sieve `1–2 mm` `Turface Proleague Elite` arcillite, autoclaved at `121°C` and oven-dried at `70°C` for `72` hours. Four `990 g` (`1.6 L`) quadrants of the **PH-04 Science Carrier (`SC`)** fill with ceramic grains and four timed-release `Nutricote` blends (`T70`, `T100`, `T180`).

- **Caption (Narrator):** *Leafy greens were sprints. Chile peppers—germination, flowering, pollination, fruit set, ripening—are a four-and-a-half-month endurance test.*

- **Panel 3 (Detail):** Chlorine-gas-sanitized seeds (`0.5 mL HCl + 30 mL bleach`, `1 h`) of *Capsicum annuum* cv. `'NuMex Española Improved'`—`12` per quadrant (`48` total)—sit anchored in guar gum.

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1 (Launch & Installation):** June 3, 2021: `SpaceX CRS-22` roars off Pad `39A`. July 12, 2021: the Flight Engineer slides the `PH-04` Science Carrier into `APH` and imbibes the four quadrants until saturated.

- **Panel 2 (Two-shot, KSC Tele-Op Console):** Gioia Massa and Matthew Romeyn watch `APH` sensor telemetry stream down to Kennedy Space Center, alongside Jacob Torres from New Mexico State University.

- **Jacob Torres:** "More than two dozen pepper varieties tested, and `'NuMex Española Improved'` won—`2,000` to `4,000` Scoville units, compact stature, packed with vitamins `C` and `K`."

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1 (Interior LED schematic):** Overhead `APH` LEDs lock onto `300 µmol/m²/s` (`16 h` light / `8 h` dark) across three pre-set canopy heights (`2.54`, `15.2`, and `35.6 cm`).

- **Panel 2 (Spectral callout):** **`27%` red, `33%` green, `40%` blue**.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "`40%` blue light shortens the internodes—keeping the pepper plants under `40` centimeters so they don't smash into the `45`-centimeter `APH` ceiling."

- **Panel 3 (Atmosphere readout):** `23°C` air, `550 ppm` CO₂ to suppress leaf intumescence, and a `Purafil` potassium-permanganate scrubber stripping ethylene out of the closed loop.

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1 (Day 14 → Day 28):** Relative humidity steps down from `80%` to `50%`, and root-zone moisture drops from `50%` to `40–45%`. On Day `28`, an astronaut opens the `APH` door and thins each quadrant down to **one** dominant plant (`20 plants/m²`).

- **Panel 2 (Day 50):** Support stands slide into the `SC` to brace the thickening stems as `APH` fans pulse to `0.9 m/s` for `5` minutes a day between `45` and `70` days after initiation (`DAI`) to shake pollen loose from the first white blossoms.

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1 (Medium shot, `Kibo`):** Megan McArthur and Thomas Pesquet gently hand-pollinate individual *Capsicum* flowers in microgravity—replacing Earth's wind and bees with human fingertips.

- **Panel 2 (Calendar tension, Day 100 → Day 120):** Originally scheduled for harvests on Days `100` and `120`, fruiting lags in microgravity. On the KSC console, Oscar Monje and Lucie Poulet extend the mission clock past Day `120`.

- **Gioia Massa:** "Fruiting takes its own time in space. Extend `PH-04` to `137` days."

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1 (Day 109 & Day 137 Harvests):** Green and glossy crimson peppers hang heavy from all four quadrants. Crew members Mark Vande Hei, Shane Kimbrough, and Kayla Barron snip **`26` edible chile peppers** across the two harvests.

- **Panel 2 (Celebration beat):** Half of the peppers go straight into spaceflight tacos—crisp, aromatic heat breaking months of thermostabilized rations. The remaining half wrap in foil and vanish into `-80°C` `MELFI` freezers.

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor: *Dissecting the Four-Quadrant Habitat*)**

- **Left Page (Page 7) — *January 2022, KSC Return (`OSD-772` / `GLDS-675`)*:** The ambient-stowed `PH-04` Science Carrier opens on the aseptic KSC bench. Christina Khodadad, Mary Hummerick, and LaShelle Spencer lift the top cover and foam layer (`Fig. 2B`), gently teasing pepper roots out of `1–2 mm` arcillite and shaking loose grains free to isolate `109` samples across **12 niches**: `stems (4)`, `root-shoot junctions (4)`, `distal roots (12)`, `rhizospheres (4)`, `bulk substrates (16)`, `wicks (16)`, `foams (12)`, `surface swabs (8)`, `leaves (4)`, `fruits (10)`, `seeds (10)`, and `water (3)` (Q1 water was dry on return).

- **Right Page (Page 8) — *Dual-Track Pipeline (`TSA`/`IMA` + `16S` `MiSeq`)*:** Half of each sample hits `OMNI` bead-ruptors (`4 mm` glass beads, `5 m/s`) and serial dilutions on `TSA`, `IMA`, `3M Petrifilm`, and `RV`/Tetrathionate *Salmonella* broths. The other `100 mg` hits liquid-nitrogen `CryoMill` (`30 Hz`, `2 min`), `DNeasy UltraClean Microbial` extraction, `V4` `16S` PCR (`Kozich` primers), and `Illumina MiSeq` (`2 × 250 bp`, `QIIME2`/`DADA2`/`SILVA 138`).

- **Spread Caption:** *Four isolated root zones. One shared cabin air loop. Every pepper, wick, and foam pad tells us how microbes travel through a 137-day fruiting habitat.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1 (Food-safety readout):** On `TSA` and `IMA`, the `PH-04` pepper fruits register from below detection limits up to just **`111 CFU/g` fresh weight** on a single Q3 pepper.

- **Panel 2 (Pathogen check):** *Escherichia coli*, *Staphylococcus aureus*, and *Salmonella* screens come back **zero across every fruit**.

- **Mary Hummerick:** "Even after `137` days in a closed chamber, the peppers are cleaner than grocery-store produce."

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1 (Science Carrier plate counts):** Beneath the canopy, the hardware tells a busier story: `SC` surface swabs average `3.2 × 10⁵` to `4.0 × 10⁴ CFU/swab` (bacteria) and `1.2 × 10⁵` to `4.9 × 10⁴ CFU/swab` (fungi), while `Q1` substrate and wicks carry significantly higher bacterial counts than `Q2–Q4` (`p ≤ 0.015`).

- **Panel 2 (Isolate IDs):** `Biolog` and `MicroSeq` identify culturable `Sphingomonas sanguinis`, `S. leidyi`, `Roseomonas cervicalis`, `Phyllobacterium`, `Cupriavidus gilardii`, `C. campinensis`, `Burkholderia contaminans`, and fungi `Phialemoniopsis curvata`, `Aspergillus`, `Exophiala`, `Purpureocillium`, and `Penicillium`.

### Act II: Fourteen in Common (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1 (Alpha diversity plots):** Anirudha Dixit displays the Shannon diversity (`H`) table from `QIIME2`. Above-surface tissues are sparse: seed, leaf, and fruit `H` all sit **`< 1.0`** (pepper fruit `0.44–0.51`, `46–194` species).

- **Panel 2 (Below-surface contrast):** Below ground, rhizosphere Shannon diversity climbs to **`1.6–2.1`** (`386–436` species—nearly double the leaves and fruits).

- **Anirudha Dixit:** "The plant filters its own canopy. Roots host the crowd; fruits stay quiet."

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1 (`Bray-Curtis` PCoA plots):** Three `PCoA` ordinations (`Adonis` `p = 0.001`) show that **tissue type** drives variation above surface, while **sample location** (wick vs. foam vs. root vs. water) drives variation below surface and across `SC` components.

- **Panel 2 (Heatmaps, `ampvis2`):** Above surface (`Fig. 6`), **`Sphingomonas`**, **`Novosphingobium`**, and **`Pseudomonas`** dominate (`> 10%` each, reaching nearly `50%` in `Q3` stems)—yet `Pseudomonas` vanishes from `Q3`/`Q4` roots and is completely absent from `SC` water.

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1 (Below-surface heatmap, `Fig. 7`):** In the roots, rhizosphere, and arcillite, **`Puia`** (a chitin- and cellulose-degrading member of the `Chitinophaga` group) emerges as a top taxon (`0–10%`) alongside `Sphingomonas`, `Pseudomonas`, `Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, `Cellulomonas`, and `Cupriavidus`.

- **Panel 2 (Hardware heatmap, `Fig. 8`):** On `SC` swabs, `Pseudomonas` hits up to `50%`, while `Leifsonia` and `Methylobacterium` peak on the wicks.

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1 (Four-way Venn diagram, `Fig. 9`):** Four overlapping ellipses—*Above Surface*, *Below Surface*, *SC Components*, and *T0 Seeds*—converge on a tiny center: **`13` named genera + `1` uncultured bacterium** (`14` total, just **`4.5%`** of the community), while `> 95%` of taxa stay niche-specific.

- **Christina Khodadad:** "Sanitized seeds still carry endophytes like `Sphingomonas`—and they meet ISS potable-water regulars like `Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, and `Cupriavidus`."

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1 (Niche-bridge schematic):** Arrows trace two-way microbial traffic: ISS cabin air deposits `Sphingomonas` on leaves; watering carries `Novosphingobium` and `Cupriavidus` down into wicks and roots; xylem and vertical transmission carry seed endophytes all the way into progeny pepper seeds.

- **Panel 2 (Caveat note):** Christina Khodadad adds a transparent note: the `SC` sat at ambient ISS temperature from November 2021 to January 2022 before Earth return, allowing post-harvest shifts in the tray components—unlike the `-80°C` `MELFI`-frozen peppers.

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1 (Wide KSC review):** The full `PH-04` team gathers around the `GLDS-675` (`OSD-772`) release dashboard (`7.55 GB`, `DOI: 10.26030/mjvk-v435`, published in *Scientific Reports* `16:12863`).

- **Panel 2 (Milestone banner):** `137` days. `26` chile peppers. Zero foodborne pathogens. `APH` officially validated for long-duration fruiting crops in microgravity.

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1 (Quiet beat, KSC high bay):** Matthew Romeyn and LaShelle Spencer walk past an `APH` ground unit. Inside, the `1–2 mm` arcillite bed looks solid and heavy.

- **Matthew Romeyn:** "`PH-04` proved we can grow fruiting peppers in arcillite for `137` days. But arcillite is single-use ceramic—heavy to launch, messy to dispose of, and it holds `40–45%` water by weight."

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1 (Flash forward):** Beside the `APH` rack sits a transparent root chamber—no clay, no rockwool, no soil. Roots hang bare in mid-air while mist nozzles and ebb-and-flow troughs pulse nutrient solution across them.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *To scale orbital farming beyond `26` peppers, NASA has to cut the substrate loose altogether—and test whether naked roots can survive microgravity.*

### Act III: Cutting the Clay Loose (Pages 19–30)

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1 (Hardware reveal):** The **Exposed Root On Orbit Test System (`XROOTS`)**, integrated directly into the ISS **Veggie** hardware—an **aeroponic and hydroponic** technology demonstration using an ebb/flow nutrient solution recovery loop.

- **Panel 2 (Sample table preview):** `n = 156` samples—plants, hardware swabs, and recirculating water—processed through the exact same `Khodadad et al., 2020` `16S` `V4` and `Zymo Quick-ITS Plus` fungal `ITS` `MiSeq` pipelines (`70 µm` cell strainers, `13,000 × g` pellets).

**Page 20**

- **Panel 1 (Contrast panel):**

  - Left: `PH-04` (`OSD-772`) — `990 g` arcillite per quadrant, `137` days, *Capsicum annuum* `'NuMex Española Improved'`, `26` peppers.

  - Right: `XROOTS` (`OSD-773`) — zero solid substrate, aeroponic/hydroponic nutrient recovery inside Veggie, `16S` + `ITS` food-safety & water-loop microbiome.

**Page 21**

- **Panel 1 (KSC archive lock):** `OSD-772` Version 2 locks its `109`-sample `16S` `MiSeq` dataset into OSDR (`29-Jan-2026`), closing the chapter on the first space-grown chile peppers.

**Page 22**

- **Panel 1 (Detail):** A single dried `'NuMex Española Improved'` seed from a space-grown Q1 pepper sits in a sterile vial—carrying vertically transmitted `Sphingomonas` from its `137`-day orbital parent.

**Page 23**

- **Panel 1 (Visual transition):** The crimson curve of a Hatch chile pepper dissolves into a web of bare white roots suspended inside a clear `XROOTS` chamber, droplets of nutrient mist clinging to root hairs in `0 g`.

**Page 24**

- **Panel 1 (Microgravity fluid physics):** In Earth gravity, mist falls and water drains. In `0 g`, surface tension wraps bare roots in thick liquid films—risking hypoxia unless ebb-and-flow recovery pulls the solution back.

**Page 25**

- **Panel 1 (Microbiology link):** On Earth (`OSD-723`), we saw how unbuffered hydroponic water amplifies `Cupriavidus` and `Sphingomonas` biofilms. In `XROOTS` (`OSD-773`), that same water loop runs in orbit.

**Page 26**

- **Panel 1 (Lab bench):** `70 µm` cell strainers filter plant debris out of `XROOTS` water and swab extracts, spinning `13,000 × g` pellets for dual `16S` (`V2 500-cycle`) and `ITS` (`V3 500-cycle`) `MiSeq` sequencing.

**Page 27**

- **Panel 1 (Crew perspective):** An astronaut inspects bare roots glowing pink under the Veggie LEDs—no dark pillows hiding what's growing beneath the canopy.

**Page 28**

- **Panel 1 (Data bridge):** `OSD-772` (`PH-04`) → `OSD-773` (`XROOTS`): from `137` days in solid arcillite to the first aeroponic/hydroponic root system in Veggie.

**Pages 29–30 (Cliffhanger Double-Page Spread: *Next Station — `OSD-773`*)**

- **Left Page (Page 29):** Inside the ISS Veggie rack, bare white plant roots hang suspended in clear `XROOTS` chambers under pink LEDs—mist droplets floating like tiny planets around the root hairs.

- **Right Page (Page 30):** Analytical telemetry overlay for **`OSD-773`**: aeroponic + hydroponic ebb/flow recovery, `n = 156` plant/swab/water samples, `16S` (`V2 500-cycle`) + `ITS` (`V3 500-cycle`) `Illumina MiSeq` food-safety & microbiome profiling.

- **Spread Caption:** *We harvested `26` chile peppers from four trays of clay. Next, we pull the clay away—and watch bare roots drink from mid-air in orbit.*

- **Cliffhanger Tag:** **NEXT VOLUME: `OSD-773` — *Exposed Root On Orbit Test System (XROOTS), an aeroponic and hydroponic plant growth system technical demonstration on the ISS*.**

## 4. Mission Debrief (Pages 31–32 Infographic Layout)

### Left Spread — Page 31: `PH-04` Flight Architecture & Environmental Controls (`OSD-772`)

| Parameter / Phase | Flight Specification (`ISS-Kibo` `APH`) | Operational Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Launch & Duration** | `SpaceX CRS-22` (`03-Jun-2021`); imbibed `12-Jul-2021`; `137` days (`2` harvests: Days `109` & `137`) | Extended from `120` days due to fruiting delay; produced `26` edible peppers |
| **Science Carrier (`SC`)** | `4` independent quadrants (`Q1–Q4`), `990 g` (`1.6 L`) `1–2 mm` arcillite + `Nutricote` | `12` seeds/quadrant (`48` total) thinned to `1` plant/quadrant (`4` total) at Day `28` |
| **Light & Atmosphere** | `300 µmol/m²/s` (`27%` R, `33%` G, `40%` B, `16:8` L:D), `23°C`, `550 ppm` CO₂, `Purafil` | `40%` blue keeps height `< 40 cm`; `550 ppm` CO₂ reduces intumescence |
| **Moisture & Pollination** | RH `80% → 50%` (Day `14`); root moisture `50% → 40–45%`; wind `0.3 → 0.9 m/s` + hand pollination | Crew hand-pollinated flowers & installed plant stands at Day `50` |

### Right Spread — Page 32: Food Safety & `16S` Microbiome Across `12` Niches (`OSD-772` + `PMC13096386`)

| Niche / Assay | Key Quantitative Result | Dominant / Notable Taxa | Spaceflight Implication |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Pepper Fruit Food Safety** | `≤ 111 CFU/g` FW (one `Q3` pepper; most `BDL`); `0` *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, *S. aureus* | `46–194` species; Shannon `H = 0.44–0.51` | `PH-04` peppers are microbiologically safe for crew consumption |
| **Above-Surface Tissues** | Shannon `H < 1.0` (seed, leaf, fruit); `1–2` in stem/RSJ; tissue type `p = 0.001` | `Sphingomonas`, `Novosphingobium`, `Pseudomonas` (`~50%` in `Q3` stem) | Canopy hosts low-diversity, tissue-filtered communities |
| **Below-Surface & `SC` Hardware** | Rhizosphere `H = 1.6–2.1` (`386–436` spp.); swabs `3.2×10⁵–4.0×10⁴ CFU/swab` | `Puia` (`Chitinophaga`), `Burkholderia`, `Ralstonia`, `Cupriavidus`, `Leifsonia` | `Pseudomonas` up to `50%` on swabs, absent in `SC` water & `Q3/Q4` roots |
| **Core Microbiome (`4`-Way Venn)** | `13` named genera + `1` uncultured (`4.5%` of total community) | `Sphingomonas` & `Novosphingobium` shared across seeds, shoots, roots, `SC` | Vertical (seed) & horizontal (air/water) transmission coexist in `APH` |

## 2. Dramatis Personae (Grounded in Study Data)

- **Dr. Ye Zhang (NASA KSC Conceptualization Lead):** Principal investigator guiding `XROOTS` biological validation—bridging microgravity fluid physics with edible multi-crop food safety.

- **Dr. Christina L. M. Khodadad (Noetic Strategies Microbiologist):** Lead author of the *Frontiers in Microbiomes* analysis; compares `XROOTS`'s un-sanitized, substrate-free multi-crop microbiome against historical Veggie pillow baselines.

- **Cory Spern, Mary Hummerick, Jennifer Gooden, Cristiana Morales, Orlando Melendez & Raymond Wheeler:** KSC science and microbiology team running `70 µm` filtration, `OMNI` bead-ruptor extractions, `TSA`/`IMA` plating, and `16S`/`ITS` `MiSeq` libraries.

- **Robert Morrow & John Wetzel (Sierra Space `XROOTS` Hardware Leads):** Engineers behind the capillary root modules, mist nozzles, and ebb-and-flow recovery loops—supported by Dan Barta, Marlin Cox, Douglas White, Guillermo Tellez, and Daniel Wyman.

- **The Exposed-Root Canopy (`6` Crops Across `4` Grow-Outs):** `'Cherry Belle'` radish, `'Little Gem'` lettuce, mizuna mustard, dwarf wheat, and `84`-day fruiting dwarf pea and tomato—their bare roots suspended in `0 g` air and mist.

- **The Un-Sanitized Multi-Crop Microbiome (`Pseudomonas`, `Trichoderma`, *Fusarium*, *Blumeria graminis*):** High-diversity communities seeded without surface sterilization (`65` unique leaf and `87` unique root bacterial genera vs. earlier Veggie tests), where `Pseudomonas` and `Trichoderma` keep opportunistic fungi in check.

## 3. 32-Page Chapter Script

### Act I: Unbolting the Baseplate (Pages 1–10)

**Page 1**

- **Panel 1 (Full-width establishing shot):** `NG-17` Cygnus approaches the International Space Station on February 19, 2022. Inside `Columbus`, astronauts unbolt the standard Veggie baseplate and bellows.

- **Panel 2 (Hardware integration):** Beneath the hanging Veggie RGB LED array, crew members mount the transparent **`XROOTS`** root-module chassis—developed by Sierra Space under NASA's NextSTEP program.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *For eight years, NASA grew space crops inside clay pillows. `XROOTS` rips the pillows away—leaving roots naked in microgravity.*

- **Panel 3 (Two-shot, KSC & Madison Payload Ops):** Ye Zhang and Robert Morrow watch live engineering cameras lock onto the clear root modules.

- **Ye Zhang:** "Two root-module configurations, three root-shoot interfaces, aerosol misting, and ebb-and-flow fluid recovery. Let's see how roots drink without gravity or clay."

**Page 2**

- **Panel 1 (Close-up, seed cartridge):** Unlike Veggie and `PH-04` (`OSD-772`), the `XROOTS` seed cartridges are loaded with **un-sanitized** seeds—a deliberate operational choice to see what a multi-crop, soil-free system carries on its own.

- **Panel 2 (Crew operation):** Every three days, an astronaut cycles the nutrient delivery and ebb-and-flow water recovery valves. Mist plumes swirl briefly inside the chamber before capillary channels draw excess droplets back into the reservoir.

**Page 3**

- **Panel 1 (Grow-out 2, `40` DAP):** Inside the `26°C`, `16:8` RGB LED glow, three crops share the `XROOTS` modules: **`'Cherry Belle'` radish**, **`'Little Gem'` lettuce**, and **mizuna mustard** (*Brassica rapa*).

- **Panel 2 (Root close-up):** White taproots and fine lateral root hairs hang suspended in misted air—no `Turface` arcillite, no `Grodan` rockwool—while radish bulbs swell cleanly at the root-shoot collar.

**Page 4**

- **Panel 1 (Grow-out 3 & Transplant into Grow-out 4):** Next come **dwarf wheat** (*Triticum aestivum*) and lettuce—and beside them, **dwarf pea** and **dwarf tomato** seedlings that are carefully transplanted into a fresh root module for Grow-out `4`, stretching all the way to **`84` days after initiation (`DAI`)**.

- **Panel 2 (Crew pollination):** Remembering `PH-04`'s lessons, ISS crew members flick and brush the yellow tomato and pea blossoms by hand— coaxing pods and red cherry tomatoes to set fruit in bare-root hydroponics.

**Page 5**

- **Panel 1 (Harvest & `MELFI` packing):** Leaves, roots, radish bulbs, pea pods, tomato fruits, wicks, nutrient solution syringes, and `ProSan`-wipe root-module swabs (taken before and after sanitization) are wrapped in sanitized foil and frozen at **`-80°C`** in `MELFI`.

- **Panel 2 (Return vehicles):** `SpaceX-26` and `SpaceX-27` carry the frozen `XROOTS` archive (`n = 156` samples) back to Kennedy Space Center.

**Page 6**

- **Panel 1 (KSC thawing & dissection):** Christina Khodadad, Cory Spern, and Mary Hummerick dissect the `XROOTS` harvests: distal upper leaves separated from proximal lower leaves, wicks, and bare roots.

- **Panel 2 (Detail, folded wheat leaf — *Frontiers* Fig. 2):** A tall dwarf wheat leaf had folded back inside its foil packet during return, touching its own lower blade—a reminder to document every physical contact point when interpreting microbial counts.

**Pages 7–8 (Double-Page Spread Anchor: *Inside the Substrate-Free Loop*)**

- **Left Page (Page 7) — *Six Crops, Zero Clay (`OSD-773` / `GLDS-676`)*:** A cutaway of the `XROOTS` dual-chamber system: mist nozzles and ebb-and-flow channels feeding bare roots of `'Little Gem'` lettuce, mizuna, `'Cherry Belle'` radish, dwarf wheat, pea, and tomato (`84` DAI). Callouts mark the exact microbial checkpoints: `nutrient solution (65–3,800 CFU/mL bacteria; 25–660 CFU/mL fungi)`, `RM1–RM2 surface swabs`, `proximal vs. distal leaves`, `wicks`, and `edible fruits/pods`.

- **Right Page (Page 8) — *Dual-Amplicon Extraction (`16S` + `ITS`)*:** Tissue homogenates (`OMNI Bead Ruptor`, `4 mm` glass beads, `5 m/s`) pass through **`70 µm` cell strainers**, spin at **`13,000 × g`** for `3 min`, and enter `Qiagen DNeasy Microbial` DNA isolation—splitting into `16S` (`V2 500-cycle` `MiSeq`) and `Zymo Quick-ITS Plus` (`V3 500-cycle` `MiSeq`, `250/251 bp`).

- **Spread Caption:** *No soil to hide in. Every microbe in `XROOTS` rides the mist, clings to the bare root, or swims through the ebb-and-flow loop.*

**Page 9**

- **Panel 1 (Culture plate readout):** On `TSA` and `IMA`, bacterial and fungal counts in the nutrient solution range from **`65` to `3,800 CFU/mL`** (bacteria) and **`25` to `660 CFU/mL`** (fungi)—peaking in Harvest `3` (`RM1`).

- **Panel 2 (Tissue gradient):** Across every crop, **distal (upper) leaves** carry lower bacterial counts than proximal leaves, wicks, and roots—and **tomato fruits and pea pods** record the lowest microbial loads of all.

**Page 10**

- **Panel 1 (Food-safety clearance):** Every screen for *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, and *Staphylococcus aureus* comes back **negative**; edible leaf and fruit counts sit squarely within Earth-grown produce ranges and prior Veggie leafy-green datasets.

- **Christina Khodadad:** "Even without solid clay or seed sanitization, `XROOTS` crops pass food-safety muster."

### Act II: Un-Sanitized Diversity & The Hidden Mold (Pages 11–22)

**Page 11**

- **Panel 1 (`16S` Diversity Comparison):** Jennifer Gooden and Cristiana Morales line up the `XROOTS` `16S` profiles against historical `2017–2018` Veggie grow-outs (`VEG-03D/E/F`).

- **Panel 2 (Contrast numbers):** Alpha diversity is still lower in leaves than in roots—but `XROOTS` carries far more unique bacterial genera: **`65` unique genera in leaf tissue** and **`87` unique genera in root tissue**, sharing only `5` leaf and `26` root genera with earlier Veggie missions!

- **Ye Zhang:** "Un-sanitized seeds plus a shared multi-crop water loop opened the door to a much richer microbiome."

**Page 12**

- **Panel 1 (Stacked bar plots):** Across the majority of `156` samples, **`Pseudomonas`** claims the highest relative abundance.

- **Panel 2 (Four-crop leaf Venn diagram — *Frontiers* Fig. 7A):** Comparing leaves of leafy greens (lettuce + mizuna), tomato, radish, and pea, **only `6` bacterial genera** are shared across all four crop types: `Pseudomonas`, `Achromobacter`, `Stenotrophomonas`, `Sphingobium`, `Rhizobium`, and `Rhodococcus`.

- **Panel 3 (Leafy-green uniqueness):** Meanwhile, lettuce and mizuna alone harbor **`48` of `70`** total leaf genera not seen in tomato, radish, or pea—including `Burkholderia`, `Mesorhizobium`, and `Sphingomonas`.

**Page 13**

- **Panel 1 (`ITS` Fungal Sequencing alert):** Orlando Melendez and Cory Spern open the `V3 500-cycle` `ITS` fungal tables.

- **Panel 2 (Two flagged names on screen):** Opportunistic *Fusarium* appears—and alongside it, **`Blumeria graminis`** (cereal powdery mildew), detected for the **first time ever on the ISS** on co-grown wheat, tomato, and pea in Grow-out `3/4`!

- **Cory Spern:** "Wait—*Blumeria graminis* powdery mildew on orbit? Did the plants crash?"

**Page 14**

- **Panel 1 (Photo check, `XROOTS` canopy):** High-resolution ISS stills show crisp green wheat, healthy pea pods, and smooth red tomatoes—**zero visible plant disease**.

- **Panel 2 (Microbial balance inset):** Co-occurring **`Pseudomonas`** and **`Trichoderma`** species—known natural antagonists of *Fusarium* and fungal pathogens—saturate the rhizosphere and phyllosphere.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "In a living, un-sanitized community, beneficial competitors can hold latent pathogens in check. Still—now we know *Blumeria* can ride up on un-sanitized seeds."

**Page 15**

- **Panel 1 (Hardware hygiene note):** Swabs from the top of the Veggie bellows show higher bacterial and fungal counts than the bottom of the bellows—highlighting where condensation and airborne spores settle in `0 g`.

- **Panel 2 (Two-shot):** John Wetzel and Robert Morrow log the engineering lessons: `XROOTS` proved bare-root aeroponics/hydroponics works in microgravity from seed to fruiting pea and tomato (`84` DAI) while cutting launch mass.

**Page 16**

- **Panel 1 (Publication milestone):** `OSD-773` (`GLDS-676`, `DOI: 10.26030/y0ng-8r17`, `4.69 GB`) and the June 15, 2026 *Frontiers in Microbiomes* paper (`PMID: 42376193`) cement `XROOTS` as the orbital baseline for substrate-free multi-crop farming.

**Page 17**

- **Panel 1 (Reflective beat, KSC):** Raymond Wheeler looks back at the Veggie rack in the SSPF high bay.

- **Raymond Wheeler:** "In `XROOTS`, we tested `6` crops under one light recipe. But before `XROOTS` ever flew—back in `2019`—we ran a very different test on **light itself**."

**Page 18**

- **Panel 1 (Color spectrum shift):** The white-pink `XROOTS` glow splits into two distinct spectral recipes: **red-heavy** vs. **blue-enriched** Veggie light arrays.

- **Caption (Narrator):** *Next in the OSDR archive, we rewind to `2019`—when `VEG-04A` and `VEG-04B` asked whether tuning red, blue, and green LEDs changes not just how mizuna mustard grows, but how it **tastes** and what microbes ride its leaves.*

**Page 19**

- **Panel 1 (Establishing shot):** Two ISS **Veggie** units (`VEG-04A` and `VEG-04B`, `2019`) glow side by side with contrasting red-to-blue-to-green LED formulations, growing **mizuna mustard** (*Brassica rapa* var. *japonica*).

## 4. Mission Debrief (Pages 31–32 Infographic Layout)

### Left Spread — Page 31: `XROOTS` Hardware & Multi-Crop Grow-Out Architecture (`OSD-773` / `GLDS-676`)

| Grow-Out / Mission | Crops & Duration | Hardware & Fluid Loop | Sampling & Sequencing Scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Launch & Setup** (`NG-17`) | Installed `Feb–Jun 2022` beneath Veggie (`baseplate`/`bellows` removed) | `2` root modules, `3` root-shoot interfaces; aeroponic mist + ebb/flow recovery | `26°C`, `16:8` RGB LEDs; watering/recovery every `3` days; un-sanitized seeds |
| **Grow-Out 2** (`40` DAP) | `'Cherry Belle'` radish, `'Little Gem'` lettuce, mizuna mustard | Bare-root mist/ebb-flow (no clay or rockwool) | Distal/proximal leaves, roots, radish bulbs, wicks, swabs, nutrient fluid |
| **Grow-Outs 3 & 4** (to `84` DAI) | Dwarf wheat + lettuce; transplanted dwarf **pea** & **tomato** (hand-pollinated) | Returned on `SpaceX-26` (`Sep 2022`) & `SpaceX-27` (`Mar–Apr 2023`) | `n = 156` samples (`MELFI` `-80°C`); `16S` (`V2`) + `ITS` (`V3`) `MiSeq` (`250/251 bp`) |

### Right Spread — Page 32: Food Safety, Bacterial & Fungal Findings (`OSD-773` + `Frontiers in Microbiomes` 2026)

| Assay / Metric | Quantitative Result | Taxonomic / Pathogen Profile | Operational Takeaway |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Nutrient Solution & Tissue CFUs** | Solution: `65–3,800 CFU/mL` bacteria; `25–660 CFU/mL` fungi (peak Harvest `3`) | Distal leaves `<` proximal leaves/wicks/roots; tomato & pea pods lowest | Edible parts match Earth & prior Veggie ranges |
| **Human Pathogen Screening** | **Negative** across all `156` samples | Zero *E. coli*, *Salmonella*, or *S. aureus* detected | Substrate-free `XROOTS` produce is safe to eat |
| **`16S` Bacterial Diversity** | `65` unique leaf & `87` unique root genera vs. `2017–2018` Veggie (`5` & `26` shared) | `Pseudomonas` dominant; `6` shared leaf genera; `48/70` unique to leafy greens | Un-sanitized seeds + multi-crop loop boost diversity |
| **`ITS` Fungal Surveillance** | First ISS detection of *Blumeria graminis* (+ *Fusarium*); **zero visible disease** | Co-occurring `Pseudomonas` & `Trichoderma` suppress pathogens | Monitor un-sanitized seed lots in closed loops |

(2024). *Pick-and-eat space crop production flight testing on the International Space Station*. *Journal of Plant Interactions*, `19(1):2292220` (`18-Jan-2024`, `DOI: 10.1080/17429145.2023.2292220`) — Taylor & Francis | DLR eLib PDF
